When iam.googleapis.com is being enabled by this module, custom-role creation can call the IAM API before enablement completes; destruction can likewise disable the API before deleting the roles. Create custom roles after the managed IAM API.

google_alloydb_user.users must wait for google_alloydb_instance.primary: AlloyDB user creation requires a provisioned primary instance, not just the cluster. The current cluster reference allows user and primary-instance creation to run concurrently. The provider's user examples explicitly order users after the primary instance. Referencing the primary instance's cluster attribute establishes this ordering and also ensures users are deleted before the instance.

aws_autoscaling_group.ng already depends on aws_iam_role.ng transitively through aws_launch_template.ng -> aws_iam_instance_profile.ng -> aws_iam_role.ng, as well as through its required policy attachments. The explicit role dependency is redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.ng references aws_launch_template.ng[each.key].id and .latest_version in its mixed_instances_policy, already establishing the launch-template dependency. The explicit depends_on entry duplicates that ordering.
aws_eks_node_group.ng references aws_iam_role.ng.0.arn in node_role_arn, so its explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.ng is redundant. Keep the separate policy-attachment dependencies.

aws_eks_fargate_profile.fargate references aws_iam_role.fargate.0.arn in pod_execution_role_arn, already establishing the role dependency. Its explicit depends_on on aws_iam_role.fargate is redundant; the policy-attachment dependency is still needed.

time_sleep.wait explicitly waits for aws_autoscaling_group.ng and aws_eks_node_group.ng, both of which already depend on aws_eks_cluster.cp. Its additional direct depends_on on aws_eks_cluster.cp duplicates that transitive ordering.

When enable_ssm is true, aws_autoscaling_group.ng launches instances whose user data installs and starts the SSM agent, but it does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm-managed. Referencing the instance profile and role does not wait for this separate attachment. Add the attachment to depends_on so the configured SSM permissions are attached before instances begin SSM registration.

When enable_ssm is true, aws_eks_node_group.ng uses user data that installs and starts the SSM agent, but no dependency orders it after aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm-managed. The node_role_arn reference only waits for the role, not this attachment. Add the attachment to depends_on so the configured SSM permissions are attached before managed instances begin SSM registration.

:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng already depends on :resource.aws_launch_template.ng through launch_template_id and latest_version references. Its explicit depends_on entry for the launch template is redundant.

:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng already depends transitively on :resource.aws_iam_role.ng through its launch template and instance profile, as well as through the required policy attachments. The explicit role dependency adds no ordering.

:resource.aws_eks_node_group.ng references :resource.aws_iam_role.ng in node_role_arn, so the explicit depends_on entry for that role duplicates an implicit dependency. Retain the policy-attachment dependencies.

:resource.kubernetes_config_map.aws-auth already waits for :resource.aws_eks_cluster.cp through its explicit dependency on aws_autoscaling_group.ng, which references the cluster. Its Kubernetes provider also references the cluster. The direct cluster depends_on entry is redundant.

:resource.time_sleep.wait already depends transitively on :resource.aws_eks_cluster.cp through its node-group, Auto Scaling group, and aws-auth dependencies. The direct cluster depends_on entry duplicates that ordering.

:resource.time_sleep.wait depends on kubernetes_config_map.aws-auth, which explicitly depends on :resource.aws_autoscaling_group.ng. The sleep's direct depends_on entry for the Auto Scaling group is therefore transitively redundant.

module.alb-ingress:resource.helm_release.albingress starts an AWS controller using the IRSA role, but does not wait for module.alb-ingress.module.irsa:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa to attach its required permissions. The referenced module.irsa ARN output depends only on role creation, so installation and policy attachment can race. Add depends_on = [module.irsa] to the release, or gate the IRSA ARN output on completion of its policy attachments.

module.app-mesh:resource.helm_release.appmesh deploys the controller using the IRSA role before module.app-mesh.module.irsa:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa is guaranteed to attach its App Mesh and Cloud Map permissions. Referencing the role ARN does not order the release after these attachments. Add depends_on = [module.irsa] to the release, or gate the IRSA ARN output on completion of its policy attachments.

module.cluster-autoscaler:resource.helm_release.autoscaler can start the autoscaler before module.cluster-autoscaler.module.irsa:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa grants the AWS permissions it needs. The role ARN output waits only for the role, not the policy attachment, permitting startup authorization failures. Add depends_on = [module.irsa] to the release, or gate the IRSA ARN output on completion of its policy attachments.

module.container-insights:resource.helm_release.containerinsights starts agents using the IRSA role without waiting for module.container-insights.module.irsa:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa to grant logging and EC2 discovery permissions. The role ARN reference does not include attachment completion, so startup can race permission setup. Add depends_on = [module.irsa] to the release, or gate the IRSA ARN output on completion of its policy attachments.
The explicit depends_on on :module.eks in :module.csi duplicates its existing implicit dependency through module.eks.cluster.name and module.eks.oidc.
aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng in node_role_arn; its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates the inferred dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng references aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng. The node group's additional explicit dependency on the same attachments is transitively redundant; retain the attachment ordering through the launch template.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups already depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng, whose role reference depends on aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its separate explicit dependency on the role adds no ordering.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng references launch-template outputs that depend on launch_template_config, which references aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng. Its explicit dependency on the instance profile duplicates this transitive data dependency.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already depends transitively on aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through its launch template and instance profile, and through the retained policy-attachment dependency. Its explicit dependency on the role is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command, already establishing the dependency duplicated by depends_on.
null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command, so its explicit dependency on kubernetes_namespace.spark is redundant.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth depends on data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which references data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and therefore module.aws_eks. Its additional explicit dependency on module.aws_eks duplicates that ordering; retain the readiness dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni already waits for module.aws_eks through data.http.eks_cluster_readiness and data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster. Its separate explicit dependency on module.aws_eks is redundant; retain the health-check dependency.

kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config depends on time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which explicitly depends on kubectl_manifest.aws_provider. The direct explicit dependency on aws_provider is redundant; retain the sleep dependency that waits for provider CRD installation.

The self-managed CoreDNS Helm installation in module.helm_addon waits for removal of the default deployment but not null_resource.modify_kube_dns. That provisioner must finish adding Helm ownership annotations and labels to the existing kube-dns Service before Helm attempts to adopt it, otherwise installation can fail with invalid ownership metadata. Add depends_on = [null_resource.modify_kube_dns] to this module call.

The Prometheus module.helm_addon installs into local.namespace_name without referencing kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus, and does not enable Helm namespace creation by default. It can therefore install before the managed namespace exists. Use the namespace resource's actual name in helm_config rather than the parallel name string.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.17.0", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.create_namespace ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus[0].metadata[0].name : local.namespace_name })

message: Argo Workflows module.helm_addon and kubernetes_namespace_v1.this independently create the same namespace: helm_config enables create_namespace but passes only a name string. If Helm creates it first, Terraform's namespace creation can fail with AlreadyExists. Reference the managed namespace in the Helm configuration so namespace creation finishes first.

When the ADOT managed add-on is enabled, aws_eks_addon.adot must wait for kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot to grant eks:addon-manager the required namespaced permissions. The existing RoleVersion tag waits only for the Role definition, not its binding, so EKS can start installation without authorization. Add the role binding to depends_on.

aws_eks_addon.adot must also wait for kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot, which grants eks:addon-manager cluster-scoped installation permissions. Referencing kubernetes_cluster_role_v1.adot in tags waits for the permission definition but not the binding that makes it effective. Add the cluster role binding to depends_on.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver reads only the IAM role ARN output of module.irsa_addon. That output depends on the role but not the separate IAM policy attachments, so the add-on can start using an unpermissioned role. When managed EBS CSI is enabled, explicitly depend on the whole module.irsa_addon to wait for its required policy attachments.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni references module.irsa_addon's role ARN output, which does not wait for the module's aws_iam_role_policy_attachment resources. When this add-on is enabled, wait for the complete module.irsa_addon so the CNI has its networking permissions before it starts using the role.

The example's eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons module enables Helm releases that wait for running pods, but its cluster ID/endpoint/OIDC references do not wait for the managed worker node group. data_plane_wait_arn is left empty, so the intended dataplane barrier is not tied to node readiness. Pass the managed node-group ARN output to data_plane_wait_arn so add-on deployment waits for the velero worker group.

module.helm_addon configures Fluent Bit with local.log_group_name, not aws_cloudwatch_log_group.aws_for_fluent_bit. When create_cw_log_group is true, the logging agent can start and create/use that group before Terraform creates it, causing an AlreadyExists race or bypassing the intended retention/encryption setup. Wire the managed log group's name into the chart values.

fix.expression: merge(local.helm_config, { values = try(var.helm_config.values, [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { aws_region = var.addon_context.aws_region_name, log_group_name = var.create_cw_log_group ? aws_cloudwatch_log_group.aws_for_fluent_bit[0].name : local.log_group_name, service_account_name = local.service_account_name })]) })

message: module.cert_manager_csi_driver defaults to namespace cert-manager with Helm namespace creation disabled, but has no ordering against module.cert_manager, which creates that namespace. When both add-ons are managed here, install cert-manager first so the CSI driver cannot fail with namespace not found.

module.cert_manager_istio_csr installs into cert-manager with create_namespace=false and relies on cert-manager to reconcile its certificate resources, but does not wait for module.cert_manager. When cert-manager is installed by this configuration, order istio-csr after it so its namespace, CRDs, and certificate controller are available.

When enable_amazon_prometheus is true, module.helm_addon sets serviceAccounts.server.create=false and uses the amp-ingest service account created by module.irsa_amp_ingest. Reading only that module's IAM role ARN does not wait for its Kubernetes service account or IAM policy attachments. Depend on the whole module.irsa_amp_ingest so the Prometheus server cannot start before its external service account and permissions exist.
aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng in node_role_arn. Its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates the implicit dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng through aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, whose depends_on includes the attachment. The additional direct depends_on duplicates that ordering; retain the attachment ordering through the launch template.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng, which references aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its separate depends_on on aws_iam_role.managed_ng is therefore transitive and redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng through the launch-template outputs and launch_template_config input. The explicit instance-profile dependency duplicates that data-reference path.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already reaches aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through the launch-template instance profile and through its retained policy-attachment dependency. The direct role depends_on is redundant.

null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command, already establishing the dependency. The explicit depends_on on the same role is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command. Its explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark duplicates this implicit dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already waits for module.aws_eks through data.http.eks_cluster_readiness -> data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster -> module.aws_eks. The separate module.aws_eks depends_on is redundant; preserve the readiness dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni already waits for module.aws_eks through data.http.eks_cluster_readiness and data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster. Its separate explicit module.aws_eks dependency is redundant; keep the readiness dependency.

kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config depends on time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which already depends on kubectl_manifest.aws_provider. The direct depends_on on aws_provider duplicates that transitive ordering.

The Grafana IRSA service account uses var.kubernetes_namespace rather than the namespace resource. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can therefore be created before kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa, failing with a namespace-not-found error. Reference the created namespace when namespace creation is enabled.

The Spark History Server IRSA service account and its namespace are created independently. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when that namespace is managed here, otherwise the service-account API request can fail.

When enabled, the CloudWatch Metrics IRSA module creates a namespace and service account without ordering them. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa to avoid creating the account in a namespace that does not yet exist.

When enabled, Fluent Bit's IRSA service account can race creation of its namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses only a namespace string and must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when this module creates it.

When enabled, ExternalDNS creates its IRSA service account independently of its namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when namespace creation is enabled, or its creation can fail.

When enabled, cert-manager's IRSA service account can be created before its namespace because metadata.namespace references only the input string. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when the namespace is managed here.

The cert-manager instance nested under OpenTelemetry has the shared IRSA namespace race: kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can run before kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Reference the created namespace when namespace creation is enabled.

When enabled, Karpenter's IRSA service account can race creation of its namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when the namespace is created here; sharing the input namespace string does not provide ordering.

When enabled, KEDA's IRSA namespace and service account have no ordering between them. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when namespace creation is enabled, otherwise the account's creation can fail.

When enabled, Velero creates its IRSA service account and namespace concurrently. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when that namespace is managed here to prevent a namespace-not-found error.

When enabled, the HAProxy ADOT collector creates an IRSA namespace and service account without ordering them. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when namespace creation is enabled.

When enabled, the Java ADOT collector's IRSA service account can be created before its namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when namespace creation is enabled to avoid an API failure.

When enabled, the Memcached ADOT collector's IRSA service account and namespace can be created concurrently. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when that namespace is managed here.

When enabled, the NGINX ADOT collector's IRSA service account has no dependency on its managed namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when namespace creation is enabled.

When enabled, AWS Private CA Issuer creates an IRSA service account independently of its namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when the namespace is managed here, otherwise service-account creation can fail.

The Prometheus Helm module uses local.namespace_name, a plain string, while kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus creates that namespace independently. module.helm_addon must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus when local.create_namespace is true; use the resultant namespace in helm_config rather than just its configured name.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.10.1", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.create_namespace ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus[0].metadata[0].name : local.namespace_name })

message: With Amazon Prometheus enabled, module.helm_addon disables creation of the Prometheus server service account and uses amp-ingest. The IAM role ARN output from module.irsa_amp_ingest only waits for its IAM role, not its Kubernetes service account or policy attachments. Wait for the whole module.irsa_amp_ingest before installing the Helm release to prevent missing-service-account startup failures.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni uses the IRSA role ARN output, which depends on role creation but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. The VPC CNI requires the attached EC2/networking permissions before activation and during teardown. Gate the add-on on the attachment, for example by making the IRSA output wait for attachments or adding depends_on on the whole irsa_addon module.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver references an IRSA role ARN but has no ordering on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. The EBS CSI driver needs these EC2 permissions to operate; the ARN output alone does not ensure they are attached. Make the IRSA output wait for attachments or depend on the whole irsa_addon module.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for kubernetes_role_v1.adot but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot. Creating a Role does not grant its permissions to eks:addon-manager; the binding must exist before EKS installs or removes the managed ADOT resources.

aws_eks_addon.adot references kubernetes_cluster_role_v1.adot but does not wait for kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot. EKS addon-manager needs the ClusterRoleBinding to receive the CRD and cluster-resource permissions before add-on provisioning and throughout deletion.

For custom namespaces with create_namespace enabled, the Cluster Autoscaler IRSA service account has no ordering on its managed namespace. kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa in that configuration. The default kube-system configuration does not need a new namespace.

If the EFS CSI driver is configured to create a custom namespace, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can run before kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa because metadata.namespace uses only the input string. Reference the created namespace in that branch; the default existing kube-system namespace needs no creation dependency.

If AWS Load Balancer Controller is installed in a custom namespace managed by IRSA, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Sharing var.kubernetes_namespace does not order their creation. The default kube-system configuration is unaffected.

module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons installs Helm workloads with wait=true, but the referenced control-plane outputs do not wait for module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups. In this example those managed nodes are the only worker capacity, so Helm can start its readiness timeout while the node group is still provisioning. Gate add-ons on managed-node-group completion; at the root, depends_on = [module.eks_blueprints] is a practical way to include that completion.

module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons starts Spark History Server against the logs/ path but only references the bucket. aws_s3_object.this creates the directory marker needed for that otherwise empty S3A log directory. Without ordering, History Server can start before the path exists and fail its log-directory check. Reference the object's bucket and key in the configured history URL.

fix.expression:
{ name = "spark-history-server", chart = "spark-history-server", repository = "https://hyper-mesh.github.io/spark-history-server", version = "1.0.0", namespace = "spark-history-server", timeout = "300", values = [yamlencode({ serviceAccount = { create = false }, sparkHistoryOpts = "-Dspark.history.fs.logDirectory=s3a://${aws_s3_object.this.bucket}/${aws_s3_object.this.key}", sparkConf = "spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.aws.credentials.provider=com.amazonaws.auth.WebIdentityTokenCredentialsProvider
spark.history.fs.eventLog.rolling.maxFilesToRetain=5
spark.hadoop.fs.s3a.impl=org.apache.hadoop.fs.s3a.S3AFileSystem
spark.eventLog.enabled=true
spark.history.ui.port=18080
", resources = { limits = { cpu = "200m", memory = "2G" }, requests = { cpu = "100m", memory = "1G" } } })] }

message: aws_s3_object.this relies on bucket-default encryption, but it can upload before aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.this configures that default. Order the object after the encryption configuration so it inherits the intended encryption even on S3 environments predating automatic SSE-S3 encryption; configuring bucket encryption later does not re-encrypt existing objects.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target can enable EventBridge delivery before aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy grants events.amazonaws.com SendMessage access. Wait for the queue policy before registering the target to avoid an initial delivery-permission failure window.

module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC objects and service accounts, but only receives the cluster ID and does not wait for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Like the aws-auth ConfigMap, these API operations should be gated on the project's explicit healthz readiness check; control-plane creation alone does not express that check's completion.
aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng through node_role_arn, so its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates an implicit dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng. Its direct depends_on on the attachment duplicates that transitive ordering.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng, which references aws_iam_role.managed_ng. The additional explicit dependency on the role is redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng references launch-template outputs. The launch template receives aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng.name through launch_template_config, already establishing a transitive dependency on the instance profile.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already waits for aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through the referenced launch template and instance profile, and through its explicit policy-attachment dependency. Its direct depends_on on the role is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command, already establishing the dependency expressed again in depends_on.
null_resource.update_trust_policy interpolates kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command, so the explicit depends_on on that namespace duplicates an implicit dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni already waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and then module.aws_eks. Its additional explicit dependency on module.aws_eks is redundant; retain the readiness dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and then module.aws_eks. Its additional explicit dependency on module.aws_eks is redundant; retain the readiness dependency.

kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config explicitly waits for time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which itself waits for kubectl_manifest.aws_provider. The direct depends_on on aws_provider duplicates that transitive dependency; retain the sleep dependency.

kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer applies an AWSPCAClusterIssuer custom resource, but does not wait for module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons to install the AWS Private CA issuer CRD. Cluster endpoint and CA ARN references do not establish this ordering, so a fresh apply can fail with an unknown resource kind. Add depends_on = [module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons].

kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer references the CA's ARN before aws_acmpca_certificate_authority_certificate.example necessarily associates its root certificate. The AWS provider documentation explicitly states that a CA cannot issue certificates before this association. Reference the association's certificate_authority_arn in the issuer manifest so issuer reconciliation and downstream certificate requests do not race CA activation.

fix.expression: yamlencode({ apiVersion = "awspca.cert-manager.io/v1beta1", kind = "AWSPCAClusterIssuer", metadata = { name = module.eks_blueprints.eks_cluster_id }, spec = { arn = aws_acmpca_certificate_authority_certificate.example.certificate_authority_arn, region = local.region } })

message: module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons consumes control-plane outputs but never waits for the managed-node-group ARN output. Its data_plane_wait_arn input remains the empty default, so the dataplane sleep is not gated on worker creation and Helm releases can start waiting for pods before workers exist. Feed module.eks_blueprints.managed_node_group_arn into the provided readiness input.

module.cert_manager_csi_driver installs its Helm release into the cert-manager namespace with create_namespace defaulting to false, while module.cert_manager creates that namespace. When both are enabled, there is no ordering between them and the CSI release can fail because the namespace does not exist. Make module.cert_manager_csi_driver depend on module.cert_manager.

When enabled alongside module.cert_manager, module.cert_manager_istio_csr installs into its cert-manager namespace with create_namespace = false and requires cert-manager certificate issuance. There is no dependency on module.cert_manager to establish the namespace, CRDs and controller first. Add an explicit dependency when this project manages both add-ons.

module.aws_privateca_issuer starts a controller that watches cert-manager CertificateRequests, but has no dependency on module.cert_manager installing those CRDs. Both are enabled in this example. Order module.aws_privateca_issuer after module.cert_manager to avoid starting the external issuer before its cert-manager API prerequisites exist.

When replacing default CoreDNS, module.helm_addon waits for null_resource.remove_default_coredns_deployment but not null_resource.modify_kube_dns. Helm and the ownership-annotation provisioner can therefore run concurrently, causing Helm to reject the existing kube-dns Service as not owned by this release. Make module.helm_addon wait for null_resource.modify_kube_dns.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for the Role definition, but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot granting that Role to eks:addon-manager. Creating the Role alone does not authorize the add-on manager to install namespaced ADOT resources. Wait for the binding before creating the add-on.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for the ClusterRole definition, but not kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot granting its permissions to eks:addon-manager. Without the binding, the add-on manager can lack permission to install ADOT CRDs and other cluster-scoped resources. Wait for this binding before creating the add-on.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni receives module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn, whose output depends only on the IAM role, not on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. The provider documentation requires the service-account role to have the add-on permissions assigned. The add-on can start using the new role before AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy is attached. Add depends_on = [module.irsa_addon] to the add-on, or gate the role ARN output on its policy attachments.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver references the IRSA role ARN output, but that output does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa to grant EBS CSI permissions. The provider documentation requires these permissions on the service-account role. Gate the add-on on module.irsa_addon completion, or gate the role ARN output on the policy attachments, so installation cannot race permission assignment.

module.helm_addon and kubernetes_namespace_v1.this both independently create the argo-workflows namespace: the Helm configuration has create_namespace = true but only uses a literal namespace name. If Helm creates it first, the Terraform namespace resource fails with AlreadyExists. Wire the managed namespace name into helm_config to serialize Helm after the namespace resource.

module.helm_addon installs Prometheus into local.namespace_name, not the already-defined local.namespace expression that references kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus. With the default enable_amazon_prometheus = false, nothing orders Helm after namespace creation and create_namespace defaults to false, so installation can fail with Namespace not found. Use local.namespace in the Helm configuration.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.17.0", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.namespace })

message: When AMP is enabled, module.helm_addon disables creation of the Prometheus server service account and expects amp-ingest from module.irsa_amp_ingest. Its role-ARN reference waits only for the IAM role, not for that module's Kubernetes service account and policy attachments. Add depends_on = [module.irsa_amp_ingest] so Helm cannot launch pods before their externally managed service account exists.

module.helm_addon configures Fluent Bit with a log-group name assembled from locals, without waiting for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.aws_for_fluent_bit. Fluent Bit has logs:CreateLogGroup permission and can start writing or create the group before Terraform creates its KMS-encrypted, retention-managed group. When create_cw_log_group is true, order the Helm deployment after this log-group resource to avoid failed logging or an AlreadyExists race.
aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates the inferred dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng. The node group's direct depends_on on the instance profile is redundant.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, whose depends_on includes aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly. The node group's direct attachment dependency duplicates that ordering; retain the launch template's attachment dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, whose depends_on includes aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy. The node group's direct attachment dependency duplicates that ordering; retain the launch template's attachment dependency.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, whose depends_on includes aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy. The node group's direct attachment dependency duplicates that ordering; retain the launch template's attachment dependency.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups already depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.managed_ng and the worker-policy attachments, all of which reference aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its direct depends_on on the IAM role adds no ordering.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng references aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng, which references aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng. The explicit ASG-to-instance-profile dependency duplicates this data-reference path.
aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through its launch template and instance profile. Its direct depends_on on the role is redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already references aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng, which explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.self_managed_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly. The ASG's direct attachment dependency is redundant; retain the launch template's dependency.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already references aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng, which explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.self_managed_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy. The ASG's direct attachment dependency is redundant; retain the launch template's dependency.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already references aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng, which explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.self_managed_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy. The ASG's direct attachment dependency is redundant; retain the launch template's dependency.

aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng already references aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng in its iam_instance_profile block. The explicit depends_on on that instance profile duplicates the inferred dependency.
aws_launch_template.self_managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through the instance profile's role reference. Its direct depends_on on the IAM role is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command. Terraform already infers the role dependency; the explicit depends_on entry is redundant.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command. The explicit depends_on on kubernetes_namespace.spark duplicates the inferred dependency.

helm_release.lb_ingress already explicitly depends on kubernetes_service_account.aws_load_balancer_controller_sa, whose annotation references aws_iam_role.aws_load_balancer_controller_role. The release's direct depends_on on the role adds no ordering.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and hence module.aws_eks. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks.cluster_id duplicates that ordering.

module.aws_eks_fargate_profiles already has an implicit dependency on module.aws_eks through eks_cluster_id. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks duplicates that dependency; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups already references module.aws_eks for the cluster ID, endpoint, CA, and security groups. Its explicit depends_on on module.aws_eks duplicates the dependency recorded by those inputs; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups already references module.aws_eks for cluster connection details and security groups. Its explicit depends_on on module.aws_eks duplicates that inferred dependency; retain the aws_auth dependency.

module.aws_eks_teams already has an implicit dependency on module.aws_eks through its eks_cluster_id input. The supplied graph records the same target for its explicit depends_on, duplicating that dependency.

module.emr_on_eks already references module.aws_eks.cluster_id and also waits for aws_auth, whose readiness check depends on the cluster. Its separate depends_on entry for module.aws_eks duplicates existing ordering; retain the aws_auth dependency.

kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar uses the same namespace name as kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks but only through a local constant. When deployed directly rather than via GitOps, the deployment can be submitted before the namespace exists. Reference the managed namespace in deployment metadata.

In the KEDA IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses var.kubernetes_namespace instead of referencing kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both resources are created concurrently when namespace creation is enabled, so the service-account request can fail with a missing namespace. Preserve the external-namespace option while referencing the namespace when managed here.

In the AMP IRSA instances, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a namespace string with no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. The ingest instance creates the namespace and can race its own service account; the query instance also needs the shared ingest namespace to exist. Wire the locally managed namespace into service-account metadata, and arrange shared-namespace ordering at the parent for the query instance.

helm_release.lb_ingress waits for the IAM role and service account, but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_role_policy. The controller can start with a role that lacks its EC2/ELB permissions, and the attachment can be removed before Helm destroys the controller. Add ordering on the policy attachment; referencing the role alone does not provide it.

helm_release.argocd_application installs Argo CD Application custom resources into the namespace created by helm_release.argocd. The supplied graph contains no dependency on that release, so installation can precede its namespace and CRDs. Use the normal helm_release.argocd reference; the source's resource.helm_release.argocd entry has not established the ordering in this graph.

module.kubernetes-addons consumes control-plane outputs from module.aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform, but those outputs do not wait for its managed node groups or aws_auth/readiness setup. In this deployment CoreDNS and Helm releases with wait=true can start before schedulable workers exist, risking insufficient-replica or Helm timeouts. Order the add-ons module after completion of the cluster-and-compute module, not just its cluster ID output.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni waits for module.aws_eks but bypasses data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, unlike aws_auth. Route this Kubernetes API write through the existing health-check barrier so it cannot run while the new API endpoint is still becoming usable.

module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC, service accounts and manifests after the AWS cluster module, but does not wait for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Its Kubernetes operations can bypass the API-health barrier already used for aws_auth. Depend on the readiness check directly rather than aws_auth, avoiding a potential dependency cycle through team configuration outputs.

When enabled, module.aws_managed_prometheus creates Kubernetes namespaces and service accounts through its IRSA modules, but its cluster-ID input does not order those operations after data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Apply the existing Kubernetes API health-check barrier to this module as well.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target references the SQS queue but not aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy. Event forwarding can become active before events.amazonaws.com has SendMessage permission, causing delivery failures during apply or teardown. Order the target after the queue policy.

kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar starts the ADOT collector independently of aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.node_groups_role_arn. When node IAM roles are supplied, attach their logging/X-Ray permissions before starting the collector, and retain those permissions until its deployment is removed; otherwise initial telemetry exports can fail.

kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config already waits for kubectl_manifest.aws_provider through time_sleep.wait_60_seconds, whose depends_on includes that provider. Remove the direct provider dependency and retain the sleep dependency.

kubectl_manifest.upbound_aws_provider_config already waits for kubectl_manifest.upbound_aws_provider through time_sleep.upbound_wait_60_seconds. The direct provider entry duplicates that ordering; retain the sleep dependency.

kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_provider_config already waits for kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_provider through time_sleep.wait_60_seconds_kubernetes. Remove the direct provider entry, retaining the sleep dependency.

kubectl_manifest.helm_provider_config already waits for kubectl_manifest.helm_provider through time_sleep.wait_60_seconds_helm. The direct provider dependency is redundant; retain the sleep dependency.

kubectl_manifest.helm_controller_config references kubernetes_service_account_v1.helm_provider, which explicitly depends on module.helm_addon. Its own depends_on on module.helm_addon duplicates this transitive ordering.

kubectl_manifest.helm_provider_clusterolebinding references kubernetes_service_account_v1.helm_provider, which explicitly depends on module.helm_addon. The manifest's direct module.helm_addon dependency is therefore redundant.

kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_controller_config references kubernetes_service_account_v1.kubernetes_controller, which explicitly depends on module.helm_addon. Its direct depends_on on module.helm_addon duplicates this ordering.

kubectl_manifest.kubernetes_controller_clusterolebinding references kubernetes_service_account_v1.kubernetes_controller, which explicitly depends on module.helm_addon. Its direct dependency on module.helm_addon is redundant.

The self-managed CoreDNS module.helm_addon waits for remove_default_coredns_deployment but not null_resource.modify_kube_dns. When migration is enabled, Helm must wait for modify_kube_dns to finish adding Helm ownership annotations and labels to the existing kube-dns Service; otherwise installation can fail because Helm cannot adopt that Service. Add an explicit dependency on modify_kube_dns.

Prometheus module.helm_addon installs into local.namespace_name, a plain string, and does not wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus. Its Helm release defaults to create_namespace=false, so installation can race namespace creation. Pass the resource-backed local.namespace instead.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.17.0", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.create_namespace ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus[0].metadata[0].name : local.namespace_name })

message: Argo Workflows module.helm_addon and kubernetes_namespace_v1.this can create the same namespace concurrently: the chart configuration enables create_namespace, while Terraform separately manages that namespace. Order Helm after the namespace resource to avoid an AlreadyExists race.

Fluent Bit module.helm_addon receives a log group name from local.log_group_name rather than aws_cloudwatch_log_group.aws_for_fluent_bit. Because the IAM policy permits logs:CreateLogGroup, running Fluent Bit before the Terraform-managed log group exists can let it create that group first, causing Terraform's creation to fail or logs to arrive before encryption and retention are configured. Reference the managed group's name in the default chart values.

fix.expression: merge(local.default_helm_config, { values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { aws_region = var.addon_context.aws_region_name, log_group_name = var.create_cw_log_group ? aws_cloudwatch_log_group.aws_for_fluent_bit[0].name : local.log_group_name, service_account = local.service_account })] }, var.helm_config)

message: aws_emrcontainers_virtual_cluster.this references the namespace but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.this. EMR registration needs the emr-containers user to have access to that namespace; creating the virtual cluster before the binding exists can fail authorization. Depend on the binding so it is also retained until virtual-cluster deletion completes.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for kubernetes_role_v1.adot through its tags, but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot. The Role alone does not grant eks:addon-manager namespace permissions. Wait for the binding before creating the ADOT add-on, and retain it during add-on deletion.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for kubernetes_cluster_role_v1.adot but not kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot. Its cluster-wide prerequisite permissions are ineffective until that binding exists, so add-on installation can race RBAC authorization. Add a dependency on the cluster role binding.

kubectl_manifest.helm_provider supplies a ControllerConfig name to its template but only depends on helm_provider_clusterolebinding. It can therefore start Crossplane provider installation before kubectl_manifest.helm_controller_config exists. Depend on the ControllerConfig manifest as well as the binding.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni references module.irsa_addon.irsa_iam_role_arn, whose output depends only on the IAM role, not its policy attachments. The VPC CNI can start using that role before AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy and any additional policies are attached. Depend on the whole module.irsa_addon (or make its role ARN output depend on the attachments).

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver consumes the role ARN output from module.irsa_addon, but that output does not wait for IAM policy attachments. Ensure module.irsa_addon is complete before starting the managed driver so its service-account role already has the required EBS permissions.

When AMP integration is enabled, Prometheus module.helm_addon sets serviceAccounts.server.create=false and uses amp-ingest, but references only module.irsa_amp_ingest's role ARN. That output waits for the IAM role, not the Kubernetes service account or policy attachments. Depend on the whole module.irsa_amp_ingest before installing the release so its required service account and permissions exist.

module.cert_manager_istio_csr installs into the cert-manager namespace with create_namespace=false and uses cert-manager Certificate resources. When both add-ons are managed here, it must wait for module.cert_manager to create the namespace and install cert-manager's CRDs/webhook; the shared addon_context does not order the two modules.

module.cert_manager_csi_driver defaults to namespace cert-manager without enabling namespace creation. When module.cert_manager is creating that namespace in this configuration, the CSI driver can race it and fail with NamespaceNotFound. Order the CSI driver after module.cert_manager; configurations using an externally installed cert-manager must supply that prerequisite separately.

Karpenter aws_cloudwatch_event_target.this can become active before aws_sqs_queue_policy.this grants EventBridge sqs:SendMessage. It references only the queue and rule, so interruption events can encounter AccessDenied during provisioning and the policy can be removed before the target during teardown. Depend on the queue policy before enabling delivery.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target references the queue but not aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy. Order target creation after the policy granting EventBridge sqs:SendMessage, preventing an active termination-event target from delivering to a queue before its permission is configured.

module.app_2048 creates an ALB Ingress but has no ordering against module.aws_load_balancer_controller. When both are enabled, the Ingress can race controller/webhook installation; on destroy, the controller can disappear before it removes the Ingress's ALB resources and finalizers. Depend on the controller module so installation precedes the sample app and controller removal follows app cleanup.

:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons already references aws_s3_object.this.key in spark_history_server_helm_config. Its explicit depends_on on :resource.aws_s3_object.this duplicates that implicit dependency, including when using -target.
aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_role.managed_ng through node_role_arn; its explicit role dependency adds no ordering.

aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng references aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng. The node group's additional explicit dependency on that attachment duplicates this transitive ordering; retain the attachment dependency on the launch template.

aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng, which already references aws_iam_role.managed_ng. Its separate explicit dependency on the role is transitively redundant.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already depends on aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng through the launch-template outputs and their launch_template_config input. The explicit instance-profile dependency duplicates that transitive path.

aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already reaches aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through its launch-template/instance-profile dependencies and through the retained policy-attachment dependency. Its explicit role dependency adds no ordering.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command. Its explicit depends_on on that role duplicates the command's implicit dependency.
null_resource.update_trust_policy references kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command. Its explicit namespace dependency duplicates that implicit dependency.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already explicitly waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which depends on data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster and then module.aws_eks. The separate explicit dependency on module.aws_eks duplicates that transitive path.

kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni already explicitly waits for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness, which reaches module.aws_eks through data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster. The additional explicit dependency on module.aws_eks is redundant.

kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config explicitly waits for time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which itself explicitly waits for kubectl_manifest.aws_provider. Its additional direct depends_on on aws_provider duplicates that ordering; retain the sleep dependency.

aws_s3_object.this relies on bucket default encryption but can be uploaded before aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration.this is applied. Waiting only at the add-ons module does not order these sibling resources. Reference the encryption configuration's bucket so the object is written after the configured encryption is in place.

:module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons consumes control-plane outputs from :module.eks_blueprints, but those outputs do not wait for its managed worker node groups. The enabled Helm releases wait for running workloads and can start their readiness timeouts before worker provisioning completes. Add an explicit dependency on the complete EKS blueprint module to ensure compute is available before installing these add-ons.

aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni receives an IAM role ARN but has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. The role output waits for the role and policy inputs, not attachment completion. The VPC CNI role must have its required permissions attached before the add-on starts using it; retain those permissions until add-on teardown completes.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver references the IRSA role ARN, but that output does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. Creating the role and policy does not grant the driver permissions until the attachment is complete. Make add-on creation and teardown depend on the attachment, for example by adding the attachment to the IRSA role output's depends_on.

aws_eks_addon.adot waits for the custom Kubernetes roles, but not kubernetes_role_binding_v1.adot. The namespaced permissions are not usable by eks:addon-manager until this binding exists, so add-on installation can race ahead and fail authorization. Wait for the binding as well as the role.

aws_eks_addon.adot references the custom cluster role's resource version but does not wait for kubernetes_cluster_role_binding_v1.adot. Creating the role alone does not grant eks:addon-manager the cluster-wide permissions needed to install the operator and its CRDs. Add a dependency on this binding.

Prometheus module.helm_addon sets serviceAccounts.server.create=false when AMP is enabled, but only consumes the role ARN from module.irsa_amp_ingest. That output does not wait for the amp-ingest Kubernetes service account or its policy attachments. Depend on the complete ingest IRSA module before installing the chart that uses its service account.

Prometheus module.helm_addon passes a plain namespace string and does not wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus. Helm namespace creation is false by default, so installation can fail with namespace not found. Use the created namespace's name in helm_config, preserving the existing-namespace branch.

fix.expression: merge({ name = local.name, chart = local.name, version = "15.10.1", repository = "https://prometheus-community.github.io/helm-charts", description = "Prometheus helm Chart deployment configuration", values = [templatefile("${path.module}/values.yaml", { operating_system = try(var.helm_config.operating_system, "linux") })] }, var.helm_config, { namespace = local.create_namespace ? kubernetes_namespace_v1.prometheus[0].metadata[0].name : local.namespace_name })

message: In the ADOT HAProxy IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a namespace string rather than kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both can be created concurrently, causing a namespace-not-found failure. Reference the namespace resource when this module creates it.

In the ADOT Java IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa has no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa despite being created inside that namespace. The shared namespace input does not order creation. Reference the created namespace's name.

In the ADOT Memcached IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can run before kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa because metadata.namespace is only an input string. Wait for the namespace this module creates to avoid namespace-not-found errors.

In the ADOT NGINX IRSA module, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa does not wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Using the same namespace input on both resources does not establish ordering, so first-apply service-account creation can fail.

The CloudWatch metrics IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a plain namespace string, so it can be created before kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa (amazon-cloudwatch by default). Reference the created namespace to order these resources.

The Fluent Bit IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa does not depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa, although its service account is created inside that namespace. Waiting for the entire IRSA module at Helm installation does not order these two internal resources.

The cert-manager IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa and kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa share an input name but have no dependency between them. The service account can be created before its namespace exists; consuming the namespace resource fixes that race.

The OpenTelemetry operator's nested cert-manager IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa does not wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. This service account requires that namespace to exist before creation; a shared namespace variable does not establish ordering.

The ExternalDNS IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses the namespace input directly rather than referencing kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. First-apply service-account creation can therefore fail because its namespace has not been created yet.

The Grafana IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can be created concurrently with kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa, because metadata.namespace is just a variable. Reference the namespace resource so the Grafana service account is not submitted before its namespace exists.

The Karpenter IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa lacks ordering after kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both resources use the namespace input independently, allowing a namespace-not-found error when creating the service account.

The KEDA IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa does not depend on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa even though it is created inside that namespace. Depend on the created namespace's name to avoid a first-apply race.

The Spark History Server IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa has no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Its namespace string can be known before the namespace exists, so service-account creation can race namespace creation.

The Velero IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa is not ordered after kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa, although the module creates both by default. Reference the created namespace instead of only the input string to prevent namespace-not-found failures.

The AWS Private CA issuer IRSA kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a namespace variable and does not wait for kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. These resources may run concurrently, causing service-account creation to fail before its namespace exists.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target activates delivery to the SQS queue but does not wait for aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy to grant events.amazonaws.com sqs:SendMessage. The queue ARN only orders queue creation, not delivery permissions. Depend on the queue policy so events are not sent before authorization is installed and the policy remains during target teardown.

module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, service accounts, and RBAC objects but does not wait for data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. This bypasses the explicit API-health gate already used for the blueprint's Kubernetes config maps. Order the teams module after the same readiness check so its Kubernetes operations do not race initial API availability.

module.aws_cloudwatch_metrics.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa uses a namespace name supplied as a string, but does not wait for module.aws_cloudwatch_metrics.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both are created by this configuration, so service-account creation can fail with 'namespace not found'. Reference the managed namespace in metadata.namespace, retaining the input name when namespace creation is disabled.

module.aws_for_fluent_bit.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can be created before module.aws_for_fluent_bit.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. The common input namespace string does not order these resources, and the Helm release's dependency on the IRSA module does not order resources inside that module.

module.cert_manager.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for module.cert_manager.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa when the namespace is managed here, as it is by default. Using var.kubernetes_namespace alone permits a namespace-not-found race.

When a custom non-kube-system namespace is configured and namespace creation is enabled, module.aws_load_balancer_controller.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for module.aws_load_balancer_controller.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. The current input-string reference does not establish that order. The default kube-system configuration does not create a namespace and is unaffected.

module.external_dns.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa has no ordering dependency on module.external_dns.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa, although its service account belongs to that managed namespace. Namespace and service-account creation can run concurrently and fail.

module.karpenter.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa should depend on module.karpenter.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. Both are created by default, but sharing var.kubernetes_namespace does not prevent the service account from being submitted before its namespace exists.

module.keda.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can race module.keda.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa because metadata.namespace references only an input string. The managed namespace must exist before the service account is created.

module.aws_privateca_issuer.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa needs an ordering dependency on module.aws_privateca_issuer.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. This configuration creates both resources, but currently allows service-account creation before namespace creation finishes.

module.velero.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa must wait for module.velero.module.helm_addon.module.irsa:resource.kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa. The namespace string shared by these resources does not express their operational ordering, leaving a namespace-not-found race.

module.aws_ebs_csi_driver:resource.aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver references the IRSA role ARN, but that output does not depend on module.aws_ebs_csi_driver.module.irsa_addon:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa. The add-on requires a role with its EBS permissions already attached; otherwise add-on provisioning and policy attachment can race. Make the add-on wait for the complete IRSA module, or make its role-ARN output depend on the attachments.

module.aws_vpc_cni:resource.aws_eks_addon.vpc_cni can start before module.aws_vpc_cni.module.irsa_addon:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.irsa finishes. The referenced role-ARN output waits for role creation, not policy attachment, while EKS requires the supplied service-account role to have the CNI permissions. Add an ordering dependency on the full IRSA module or include attachment completion in the role-ARN output's dependencies.

With Amazon Prometheus enabled, module.prometheus.module.helm_addon:resource.helm_release.addon sets serviceAccounts.server.create=false and uses the amp-ingest service account created by module.prometheus:module.irsa_amp_ingest, but does not wait for that module to complete. Passing its role ARN does not order service-account creation or policy attachment. Wait for the complete ingest IRSA module before installing the chart to avoid pods starting without their required service account and permissions.

module.crossplane:resource.kubectl_manifest.aws_provider_config explicitly depends on module.crossplane:resource.kubectl_manifest.aws_provider, but already waits for time_sleep.wait_30_seconds, which explicitly depends on that same provider manifest. Remove only the direct aws_provider entry; retain the sleep dependency and its CRD-readiness delay.

:module.adot_collector_java installs the otel-config collector chart, which uses the OpenTelemetryCollector custom resource supplied by :module.opentelemetry_operator. When installing both into a fresh cluster, the collector must wait for the operator's CRDs and admission webhook to be installed and ready. There is currently no ordering between these modules; add depends_on = [module.opentelemetry_operator] to the collector module. If the operator is managed externally, its readiness must instead be ensured externally.

:module.adot_collector_haproxy installs the otel-config collector chart and needs the OpenTelemetryCollector CRD and admission webhook installed by :module.opentelemetry_operator. These modules currently run independently, so a fresh-cluster apply can submit the custom resource before its API exists. Order the collector module after the operator module when Terraform manages both.

:module.adot_collector_memcached needs the OpenTelemetryCollector CRD and admission webhook supplied by :module.opentelemetry_operator before its otel-config chart can be installed. No dependency orders these modules, permitting a missing-CRD or unavailable-webhook failure when both are enabled on a fresh cluster. Make the collector depend on the operator module.

:module.adot_collector_nginx installs the otel-config collector chart but does not wait for :module.opentelemetry_operator, which supplies its OpenTelemetryCollector API and admission webhook. Order the collector module after the operator module when deploying both, so its custom resources are not submitted before the operator installation is ready.

With the default opentelemetry-operator chart certificate configuration, :module.opentelemetry_operator requires cert-manager's Certificate/Issuer APIs and webhook, supplied by :module.cert_manager. If Terraform installs both into a fresh cluster, the operator module must wait for the cert-manager module. No dependency currently enforces this. This ordering is unnecessary only when cert-manager is already installed externally or chart overrides disable its use.

module.aws_node_termination_handler:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.aws_node_termination_handler_rule_target activates delivery to the SQS queue without waiting for module.aws_node_termination_handler:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.aws_node_termination_handler_queue_policy, which authorizes events.amazonaws.com to send messages. Order target registration after policy installation so newly matched termination events are not delivered before the queue grants access; the queue-ARN reference alone does not express this permission dependency.

:resource.kubernetes_config_map.amazon_vpc_cni explicitly depends on :module.aws_eks, but its retained dependency on :data.http.eks_cluster_readiness already reaches :module.aws_eks through :data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster. Remove the direct module dependency while retaining the readiness check.

:resource.kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth explicitly depends on :module.aws_eks, but :data.http.eks_cluster_readiness already depends on :data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster, which depends on :module.aws_eks. The direct module dependency duplicates this ordering; retain the readiness dependency.

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng already references module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.managed_ng through node_role_arn. Its explicit dependency on that same IAM role is redundant.

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups already waits for module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.managed_ng through its explicit dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng, whose role attribute references the IAM role. The additional direct role dependency is redundant.

module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng references aws_launch_template.managed_node_groups, which explicitly depends on module.aws_eks_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.managed_ng. Its direct dependency on the attachment duplicates that transitive ordering. Retain the launch template's attachment dependency if removing this edge.

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already depends on module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.self_managed_ng through the launch-template outputs, the launch-template resource, and its launch_template_config input containing the instance-profile name. Its explicit instance-profile dependency is redundant.

module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.self_managed_ng already reaches module.aws_eks_self_managed_node_groups:resource.aws_iam_role.self_managed_ng through both its launch-template/instance-profile data references and the retained dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.self_managed_ng. Its direct IAM-role dependency adds no ordering.

module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy already references module.emr_on_eks:resource.aws_iam_role.emr_on_eks_execution.id in its local-exec command. Terraform infers the role dependency from that interpolation, so the explicit depends_on entry duplicates it.

module.emr_on_eks:resource.null_resource.update_trust_policy already references module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_namespace.spark.id in its local-exec command. Its explicit dependency on that namespace is therefore redundant.

:module.aws_eks_teams creates Kubernetes namespaces, RBAC objects, and manifests without waiting for :data.http.eks_cluster_readiness. Its cluster-ID input orders cluster provisioning but does not include the project's explicit Kubernetes API health check. Add a dependency on the readiness data source so team resources cannot race API readiness, as the root ConfigMaps are already protected against.

module.aws_eks_teams:resource.kubernetes_cluster_role_binding.team names the ClusterRole managed by module.aws_eks_teams:resource.kubernetes_cluster_role.team using a reconstructed string. No dependency orders the binding after its referenced role or preserves the reverse teardown order. Reference the managed ClusterRole's name in the role_ref block.

module.aws_eks_teams:resource.kubernetes_role_binding.team refers to the Role managed by module.aws_eks_teams:resource.kubernetes_role.team only through the string "${each.key}-role". Their shared namespace dependency does not order them relative to one another. Reference the managed Role's name so the binding follows role creation and precedes role destruction.

module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_role_binding.emr_containers uses local.emr_service_name for its role_ref rather than referencing module.emr_on_eks:resource.kubernetes_role.emr_containers. Both wait for the namespace, but neither waits for the other, allowing the binding to precede its Role and leaving teardown unordered. Use the managed Role's name in role_ref.

:data.aws_iam_policy_document.eks_key constructs the cluster IAM-role principal from its expected ARN instead of referencing the role created by :module.aws_eks. Consequently, the KMS key consuming this document can be created before that principal exists, causing KMS to reject the policy as containing an invalid principal. Reference the module's cluster_iam_role_arn output in the principal identifiers to order policy consumption after role creation. Use the role output rather than a broad depends_on on the EKS module, since the cluster itself consumes the KMS key.

aws_elasticsearch_domain.opensearch uses vpc_options but has no dependency on aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch. The Elasticsearch service-linked role must exist before provisioning a VPC domain; the provider documentation explicitly requires this ordering when both are created together. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_service_linked_role.opensearch], which also handles the role's optional count.

The node group's separate depends_on on the same attachments adds no ordering beyond that path; retain the attachment dependency on the launch template if removing this edge.

kubernetes_config_map.aws_auth already waits for module.aws_eks through data.http.eks_cluster_readiness -> data.aws_eks_cluster.cluster -> module.aws_eks. The additional explicit dependency on module.aws_eks adds no ordering beyond the readiness path.

kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa has no dependency on kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa even though the ingress-nginx IRSA configuration creates both. The shared namespace string does not order creation, so service account creation can fail before the namespace exists.

kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa can run concurrently with kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa in the Karpenter IRSA module, which creates both by default. Its namespace must exist first; using only var.kubernetes_namespace does not establish that prerequisite.

When KEDA creates IRSA, kubernetes_service_account_v1.irsa and kubernetes_namespace_v1.irsa are created without an ordering edge. The service account uses only the namespace input and may fail if created first. Select the namespace resource's name when the module manages the namespace.

kubernetes_deployment.aws_otel_eks_sidecar uses the same configured namespace string as kubernetes_namespace.aws_otel_eks but does not depend on it. When enabled, the Deployment can be created before its namespace and fail. Reference the namespace resource in the Deployment metadata.

helm_release.argocd_application has no effective dependency on helm_release.argocd in the supplied graph. The Argo CD release installs the Application CRD and creates the argocd namespace, so installing the application chart concurrently can fail. Correct the source's resource.helm_release.argocd dependency to helm_release.argocd, or establish a data reference through namespace.

kubernetes_secret.argocd_gitops has no effective dependency on helm_release.argocd in the supplied graph, although the Helm release creates its argocd namespace. With AMP enabled, helm_release.prometheus sets serviceAccounts.server.create=false and uses the amp-ingest service account created by module.irsa_amp_ingest. Its namespace dependency does not wait for that module's service account or IAM policy attachments. Add a dependency on module.irsa_amp_ingest so Prometheus does not start without its managed identity and remote-write permissions; referencing only the module's role ARN would not cover those prerequisites.

module.kubernetes-addons consumes only cluster/workspace outputs from module.aws-eks-accelerator-for-terraform; those outputs do not wait for the managed node groups. The enabled Helm charts wait for running workloads and can time out while the initial worker capacity is still provisioning. Order the add-ons after the accelerator module's worker provisioning, for example with a root-level depends_on on that module.

Order target registration after the queue policy to avoid an initially unauthorized event-delivery window.
