Wire storage_container_name through the storage account module's containers output for managed containers, or add explicit ordering at the root module calls.

aws_iam_instance_profile.instance adds a role using local.aws_iam_role_instance_name, which does not reference aws_iam_role.instance. With create_runner_iam_role enabled, profile creation can attempt to add the role before it exists. Reference the managed role directly.

aws_iam_role_policy.instance uses a computed role name rather than referencing aws_iam_role.instance. Both resources are created when logging and managed-role creation are enabled, so PutRolePolicy can run before the role exists.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy references the policy but identifies aws_iam_role.instance only through an independently computed name. Attaching the policy can race creation of the role.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance attaches the cache policy to the runner-agent role, but its computed role name does not order it after aws_iam_role.instance. Reference the managed role when enabled, retaining the external-role fallback.

When enabled alongside managed-role creation, aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eip can attempt to attach its policy before aws_iam_role.instance exists. Their shared computed name creates no resource dependency.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_session_manager_policy uses an independently computed role name and can attach its policy before aws_iam_role.instance is created. Preserve support for an externally managed role with a conditional reference.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_session_manager_aws_managed has no dependency on aws_iam_role.instance despite attaching AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore to that role when managed-role creation is enabled. The attachment can run before the role exists.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role attaches to aws_iam_role.instance using only a computed name. With both options enabled, Terraform can attempt the attachment before role creation completes.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm references the SSM policy but not aws_iam_role.instance, whose computed name it uses. Attaching the policy can therefore race creation of the managed runner-agent role.

aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.user_defined_policies can attach supplied policies before aws_iam_role.instance exists because role is only an independently computed string. Reference the managed role conditionally so externally managed roles remain supported.

aws_launch_template.gitlab_runner_instance specifies its instance-profile name through local.aws_iam_role_instance_name, without referencing aws_iam_instance_profile.instance. Consequently the downstream Auto Scaling group can launch before the managed profile exists. Reference the profile's name in the iam_instance_profile block, preserving the external-profile case.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance immediately launches a runner agent, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy. An instance profile alone does not ensure the agent has the EC2 and iam:PassRole permissions needed to provision Docker machines. Order instance launch after this attachment when it is enabled.

When token management is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start its user-data registration script before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm grants Parameter Store access. Wait for the attachment before launching the agent so bootstrap token reads/writes are authorized.

With EIP assignment enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can run the EIP user-data snippet before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eip grants the required permissions. The EIP resource's existence does not order launch after the policy attachment; wait for the attachment before bootstrapping the agent.

With managed-role CloudWatch logging enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start its logging bootstrap before aws_iam_role_policy.instance has granted logging permissions. Wait for the inline policy before launching the agent to avoid unauthorized initial log delivery.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance starts a runner that can immediately accept jobs using the configured S3 cache, but it does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance. Cache bucket/policy creation alone does not grant access to the agent role; order launch after the cache-policy attachment when present.

When service-linked-role creation is allowed, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start provisioning Spot Docker machines before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role grants the agent permission to create the required service-linked role. Wait for this attachment before starting the agent, especially in accounts where that service-linked role does not yet exist.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can run the registration user-data script before aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token has been initialized. The script uses an independently constructed parameter name and manages its value, so parallel creation can either encounter a missing parameter or race Terraform's initial value="null" write. Create the parameter before launching the agent.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance passes an independently computed Sentry parameter name to bootstrap without waiting for aws_ssm_parameter.runner_sentry_dsn. When bootstrap reads or updates this parameter, it can race Terraform's placeholder creation. Initialize the managed parameter before launching the agent.

When CloudWatch logging is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance configures the log group by a separately computed name and can start log delivery before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment exists. Ensure the managed log group, including retention and optional KMS configuration, is created before agent bootstrap.

For the docker+machine executor, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance starts the agent that provisions and connects to Docker machines, but it does not wait for aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_ssh_runner. Referencing security groups does not ensure this separate SSH ingress rule exists; install it before the agent can provision workers.

For the docker+machine executor, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start accepting jobs before aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_docker_runner permits the agent to reach worker Docker daemons on TCP 2376. Group creation alone does not include this separately managed ingress rule; order launch after the rule.

aws_lambda_function.terminate_runner_instances references its execution role but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.lambda to grant EC2 termination, lifecycle completion, and log-write permissions. The function can become an EventBridge target before those permissions exist. Add ordering after the attachment; its policy dependency also ensures the managed Lambda log group exists first.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.terminate_instances can begin delivering termination events before aws_lambda_permission.unqualified_alias_triggers allows EventBridge to invoke the function. The target uses the unqualified function ARN, so it should wait specifically for the unqualified permission, not merely the published-version permission.

aws_autoscaling_lifecycle_hook.terminate_instances can activate termination lifecycle events before aws_cloudwatch_event_target.terminate_instances has connected those events to the cleanup Lambda. A termination in that window can time out with CONTINUE without cleaning up worker instances. Create the event target and its invocation prerequisites before enabling the hook.

In the supplied graph, null_resource.file_permission does not depend on local_file.private_ssh_key, so its chmod command can run before the private key file exists. The source already contains the correct depends_on; preserve that dependency and reconcile the graph with the source.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance launches the runner agent without waiting for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy. Its instance-profile reference waits for the role, not its policy attachments, so the runner can start accepting jobs before it has permission to provision Docker Machine instances. Order instance launch after this attachment; this does not by itself guarantee IAM propagation has completed.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance so the runner agent's cache permissions are attached before it starts processing jobs. Referencing the instance profile does not order this separate attachment before instance launch.

When service-linked-role creation is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role. Otherwise the runner can attempt its first Spot provisioning operation before the permission to create the necessary service-linked role is attached. The instance-profile dependency does not cover this attachment.

When token management is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm. The instance's user-data manages the runner token in Parameter Store, but the ASG can launch it before the SSM permissions are attached to its role.

When CloudWatch logging is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_iam_role_policy.instance. Its bootstrap configures logging, but the separate inline logging policy can still be pending when the instance starts; the instance-profile reference only orders creation of the role and profile.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token before launching the instance whose user-data manages that parameter's value. Both use the same locally constructed name without a resource dependency. Concurrent initialization can cause ParameterAlreadyExists if user-data creates it first, or a race between the initial null value and the registered token.

When logging is enabled, aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment. Bootstrap enables logging using the environment name, but no reference orders the Terraform-managed log group before the agent starts. The agent can encounter a missing group or create it before Terraform does, causing a creation conflict.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_ssh before starting the runner service. Its Docker Machine executor needs SSH access to provision workers, but the user-data dependency on the worker security group's name does not wait for the separately managed SSH rule.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_docker before starting the runner service. The Docker Machine executor connects to workers on TCP 2376, but the existing reference to the worker security group does not order this separate ingress rule before the runner can accept jobs.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for aws_security_group_rule.out_all before starting the Docker Machine executor. Worker provisioning and builds require outbound connectivity, while the worker security group has its egress supplied only by this separate rule. Referencing the group in runner configuration does not wait for the egress rule.

The source for local_file.public_ssh_key explicitly declares depends_on = ["tls_private_key.ssh"], but its content already references tls_private_key.ssh.public_key_openssh. The implicit dependency shown in the graph supplies the same ordering, so the source-level depends_on is redundant. Note that this explicit edge is absent from the supplied graph's depends_on_deps.

data.template_file.gitlab_runner supplies the SSM parameter name to instance bootstrap using a shared local rather than aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token.name. Consequently, the Auto Scaling group can launch bootstrap before Terraform initializes the parameter. Bootstrap reads or updates this parameter, so concurrent initialization can cause a missing-parameter failure, a creation conflict, or an overwrite of the registered token. Reference the managed parameter name in the template variables.

fix.expression:
{
  gitlab_runner_version = var.gitlab_runner_version
  docker_machine_version = var.docker_machine_version
  runners_config = data.template_file.runners.rendered
  runners_executor = var.runners_executor
  pre_install = var.userdata_pre_install
  post_install = var.userdata_post_install
  runners_gitlab_url = var.runners_gitlab_url
  runners_token = var.runners_token
  secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key = aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token.name
  secure_parameter_store_region = var.aws_region
  gitlab_runner_registration_token = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["registration_token"]
  giltab_runner_description = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["description"]
  gitlab_runner_tag_list = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["tag_list"]
  gitlab_runner_locked_to_project = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["locked_to_project"]
  gitlab_runner_run_untagged = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["run_untagged"]
  gitlab_runner_maximum_timeout = var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["maximum_timeout"]
}

message: data.template_file.logging configures logging using var.environment, while aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment independently creates the log group with that name. There is no dependency ensuring the managed log group exists before the resulting user data starts logging. Reference its name when logging is enabled to order instance launch after log-group creation and avoid startup failures or a conflict if the logging agent auto-creates the group.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can launch instances before aws_iam_role_policy.instance installs their CloudWatch Logs permissions. The launch configuration depends on the role through its instance profile, but that does not order creation of the separate inline policy. When logging is enabled, wait for the policy before launching instances so bootstrap logging has its required permissions.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can launch bootstrap before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm attaches the parameter-store permissions to the instance role. Its dependency on the instance profile does not include this separate attachment. When token management is enabled, order launch after this attachment so bootstrap can read and store the registration token. This ordering does not itself guarantee completion of IAM propagation.

aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start the runner and accept jobs before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance grants its role access to the configured S3 cache. Referencing the instance profile orders creation of the role, not its policy attachments. Order the Auto Scaling group after this attachment so initial jobs do not race cache-permission installation; IAM propagation may still require retries.

In the supplied graph, :resource.null_resource.file_permission is not ordered after :resource.local_file.private_ssh_key, so its local-exec chmod can run before the private-key file exists. key.tf already shows the appropriate explicit depends_on; retain it and ensure it is represented in the effective graph. Alternatively, use file-derived triggers to establish the ordering and rerun chmod when key content or the filename changes.

module.runner:data.template_file.gitlab_runner supplies the SSM parameter name from a local string rather than referencing module.runner:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token. Consequently, the ASG can start user-data before Terraform creates the parameter that user-data manages. This can race token reads/writes or parameter creation. Populate the template variable from the managed parameter's name to order the downstream launch after parameter creation.

fix.expression:
{
  gitlab_runner_version                   = "${var.gitlab_runner_version}"
  docker_machine_version                  = "${var.docker_machine_version}"
  runners_config                          = "${data.template_file.runners.rendered}"
  runners_executor                        = "${var.runners_executor}"
  pre_install                             = "${var.userdata_pre_install}"
  post_install                            = "${var.userdata_post_install}"
  runners_gitlab_url                      = "${var.runners_gitlab_url}"
  runners_token                           = "${var.runners_token}"
  secure_parameter_store_runner_token_key = "${aws_ssm_parameter.runner_registration_token.name}"
  secure_parameter_store_region           = "${var.aws_region}"
  gitlab_runner_registration_token        = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["registration_token"]}"
  giltab_runner_description               = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["description"]}"
  gitlab_runner_tag_list                  = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["tag_list"]}"
  gitlab_runner_locked_to_project         = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["locked_to_project"]}"
  gitlab_runner_run_untagged              = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["run_untagged"]}"
  gitlab_runner_maximum_timeout           = "${var.gitlab_runner_registration_config["maximum_timeout"]}"
}

message: module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance launches a runner immediately (desired_capacity = 1), but its instance-profile reference only waits for the role/profile, not module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.instance_docker_machine_policy. The runner can start accepting jobs before it has permission to provision Docker Machine workers. Order ASG creation after this attachment; ordering does not by itself eliminate IAM propagation delays.

module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance has no dependency on module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.docker_machine_cache_instance. The runner can start handling builds before its cache-access policy is attached, causing initial cache operations to fail. Wait for this attachment before launching the runner.

When service-linked-role creation is enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance should wait for module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.service_linked_role. Otherwise the runner can attempt to provision Spot workers before receiving the permission intended to create the required service-linked role in an account where it does not yet exist.

When token management is enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can execute its token-management user-data before module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm grants the instance role SSM access. Referencing the instance profile does not wait for policy attachments. Order the ASG after this attachment to avoid bootstrap AccessDenied failures.

With CloudWatch logging enabled, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start the logging agent before module.runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.instance installs its logging permissions. The role/profile dependency does not include this inline policy. Wait for the policy before launching instances to avoid initial logging authorization failures.

module.runner:data.template_file.logging identifies the logging environment using only var.environment, so the downstream runner launch does not wait for module.runner:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.environment. With logging enabled, the agent can start before its managed log group exists, causing failed initial writes or an auto-creation race with Terraform. Reference the managed group's name in the template variables while preserving the disabled-logging case.

For the configured docker+machine executor, module.runner:resource.aws_autoscaling_group.gitlab_runner_instance can start accepting jobs before module.runner:resource.aws_security_group_rule.docker_machine_ssh is installed. Order this add-on after create_calico_installation, and ensure that the installation provisioner waits for Calico readiness rather than merely submitting the Installation object. This also orders the downstream Karpenter deployment after CNI installation.

:resource.aws_lambda_permission.forge_trust_validator_lambda already transitively depends on :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda: source_arn references the EventBridge rule, whose depends_on includes that module. The permission's direct depends_on on the module adds no ordering.

:resource.null_resource.update_forge_role_trust must wait for :module.forge_trust_validator_lambda to create its execution role. The local-exec provisioner submits a trust policy whose AWS principal is the manually constructed validator role ARN; IAM validates that principal, so running before the module creates the role can fail with an invalid-principal error. The constructed ARN does not establish a dependency on the module. Add depends_on, or refactor the principal in local.lambda_trust_statement to use the module's lambda_role_arn output.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.forge_trust_validator_lambda should depend on :resource.aws_lambda_permission.forge_trust_validator_lambda so the enabled scheduled rule does not begin invoking its Lambda target before events.amazonaws.com has invocation permission. The provider documentation requires this permission for EventBridge invocation, but the target and permission currently can be created concurrently. Add depends_on on the permission to avoid this invocation-readiness race.

helm_release.karpenter explicitly depends on module.eks, but its values already reference module.eks.cluster_name and module.eks.cluster_endpoint. The supplied graph therefore already establishes this dependency implicitly; remove the duplicate depends_on entry.

helm_release.karpenter deploys a controller whose credentials come from EKS Pod Identity (module.karpenter enables create_pod_identity_association), but it has no dependency on aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent. Creating the association does not install the credential-serving agent. The controller can therefore start before the agent is available and fail AWS authentication. Order the release after the Pod Identity agent add-on; that also orders it after the bootstrap node group, on which the add-on already depends.

helm_release.karpenter explicitly depends on null_resource.wait_for_cluster, but that ordering is already established transitively: helm_release.karpenter references module.karpenter, which depends on null_resource.patch_calico_installation, which references data.external.update_kubeconfig, which explicitly depends on null_resource.wait_for_cluster. helm_release.karpenter launches a controller whose service account uses the EKS Pod Identity association enabled in module.karpenter, but it has no dependency on aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent. The release and agent add-on can therefore be installed concurrently, allowing the controller to start before its AWS credential agent is available. Make the release depend on aws_eks_addon.eks_pod_identity_agent to establish that operational prerequisite; this also orders it after the self-managed node group.

time_sleep.wait_30_seconds should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_integration so the delay begins after the integration's inventory permissions are attached. Currently the policy and sleep can run concurrently after role creation, allowing signalfx_aws_integration.integration to become enabled before these permissions are installed or have had the intended propagation delay. Make the sleep wait for both inline policies; policy-hash triggers also rerun the delay when permissions change.

time_sleep.wait_30_seconds should depend on aws_iam_role_policy.splunk_managed_policy so the delay starts after the metric-stream permissions are attached. signalfx_aws_integration.integration enables use_metric_streams_sync, whose documented requirements include the CloudWatch metric-stream actions and iam:PassRole provided by this policy. Waiting only for the role allows the delay to finish and the integration to activate before this policy is ready. Make the sleep wait for both inline policies; policy-hash triggers also rerun the delay when permissions change.

Creating the function does not wait for this policy; AWS can reject creation of the SQS mapping if the role lacks ReceiveMessage, DeleteMessage, or GetQueueAttributes permissions. The SQS service-principal Lambda permission is not a substitute for execution-role permissions.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_permission.scale_down before attaching the enabled schedule to the function. Both currently wait only for the rule and function, so a scheduled invocation can occur before EventBridge is authorized to invoke Lambda.

module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_permission.pool. Attaching a target to an enabled schedule allows invocations immediately, but no dependency ensures the corresponding EventBridge invoke permission exists first.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_permission.syncer. The shared references to the rule and function do not order these siblings, allowing an enabled schedule to attempt invocation before Lambda grants EventBridge permission.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down before enabling scheduled execution. Function creation waits for the execution role but not this separately managed policy, so the first scale-down execution can lack its GitHub credential/EC2 access.

module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool. Otherwise the enabled schedule can execute pool adjustment before the execution role receives the policy needed to read credentials/configuration and launch runners.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. The enabled schedule can invoke the syncer as soon as the target is attached, whereas function creation does not wait for this separate policy granting access to the distribution object.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. Uploading this object deliberately invokes the syncer after deployment, but the existing notification dependency waits only for invoke permission and function creation, not the execution role's S3-access policy. The initial synchronization can therefore fail with AccessDenied.

module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy is intended for module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq, but queue_url currently references the main build queue. It therefore has no dependency on the DLQ and applies a second policy to the wrong queue. Reference the DLQ URL so Terraform both orders the resources and applies the transport policy to the intended queue.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms when a distribution KMS key is configured. The upload triggers the syncer immediately, but neither the function reference nor the notification dependency waits for the execution role's KMS permissions needed to write the encrypted distribution.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms when the distribution uses a KMS key. Otherwise the enabled schedule can execute synchronization before the execution role has the required KMS permissions.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging. This upload deliberately invokes the function; without ordering it after the logging policy, the first synchronization can run before its log group and log-write permissions are ready.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging, which also waits for the managed log group. The enabled schedule can currently invoke the function before its logging infrastructure and permissions are provisioned.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down_logging. This also orders the target after the managed log group; otherwise scheduled invocations can start before log-write permissions and the log group are ready.

module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging. The policy depends on the managed log group, so this ordering prevents scheduled pool executions before logging resources and permissions are available.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up_logging. The mapping defaults to enabled and can process queued events as soon as it is created, while the function reference does not wait for the log group or the separately managed log-write policy.

module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook before registering/enabling the GitHub App webhook. The endpoint is constructed from the API object and a literal path, so its availability does not imply the $default stage exists. Gate the exported endpoint on stage creation (or add an appropriate module-level ordering dependency) to avoid directing GitHub events to an endpoint not yet serving requests.

module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_route.webhook. The exported webhook endpoint references the API and a literal relative path, not the POST route or its integration. The provisioning script can therefore configure GitHub to deliver events before the receiving route exists; gate the endpoint output on route readiness.

module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_permission.webhook before configuring GitHub delivery. The webhook endpoint output does not wait for API Gateway's Lambda invoke permission, so GitHub events can arrive while the API cannot yet invoke the handler. Carry this readiness dependency through the webhook endpoint output or an appropriate module dependency.

module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_ssm before it becomes reachable through the API integration. Its execution-role reference does not wait for this policy, which is required to read the webhook secret named in the function environment; early deliveries can otherwise fail authorization while the policy is still being created.

module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_sqs before the API integration can expose it. The handler publishes accepted events to the queues in RUNNER_CONFIG, but the role reference alone does not wait for the separate SQS publishing policy, allowing early requests to fail with AccessDenied.

When AMI lookup through SSM is configured, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read. The enabled SQS mapping can invoke scale-up immediately after function creation, but neither the function nor mapping waits for the attachment that permits reading AMI_ID_SSM_PARAMETER_NAME.

When AMI lookup through SSM is configured, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read. Referencing config containing the policy ARN only waits for the policy itself, not its attachment to the pool execution role; scheduled pool execution can otherwise fail to read the configured AMI parameter.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_config_run_as. Runner bootstrapping discovers the SSM configuration directory through the ghr:ssm_config_path tag, which is assembled from variables rather than parameter references. Without this ordering, scale-up can use the template and launch prebuilt runners before their run_as setting exists.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_agent_mode. Runner startup discovers agent_mode under the variable-derived ghr:ssm_config_path tag; no data reference ensures this configuration is created before the launch template becomes available to the scale-up/pool functions.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.jit_config_enabled. The runner's enable_jit_config parameter is located through the configuration-path tag rather than a resource reference, allowing instances launched through scale-up to start before this bootstrap setting is provisioned.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_enable_cloudwatch. Runners discover enable_cloudwatch via the ghr:ssm_config_path tag, but sharing the same path variables does not order its creation before scale-up can launch instances from the template. This remains relevant with prebuilt AMIs and enable_userdata=false.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.token_path. Runner startup resolves token_path beneath the configuration directory carried in an instance tag; the template has no reference to this parameter. Ordering the template after the parameter prevents scale-up/pool from launching runners before the token-location configuration exists.

When the optional workflow-job queue is enabled, module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_workflow_job_sqs. The function advertises the queue in its environment and can become reachable through API Gateway before this separate publishing policy has been applied to its execution role.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_parameters. The launch template references the instance profile and role, but not the separate policy granting runners access to their bootstrap configuration and registration tokens. Scale-up can therefore launch instances before the permissions needed for startup are installed.

When create_service_linked_role_spot is enabled, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.service_linked_role. This example enables that option and uses Spot capacity; the mapping can currently start scale-up before the execution role receives permission to create the Spot service-linked role, causing the first launch to fail in accounts where that role does not already exist.

When CloudWatch agent support is enabled, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.cloudwatch. A reference to the agent configuration parameter does not wait for the separate instance-role policy granting permission to read it and publish telemetry. Without this ordering, dynamically launched runners can bootstrap before those permissions are attached.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up does not wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up, which grants its execution role access to the build queue. Referencing the Lambda function only orders creation of the role, not attachment of this policy. Creating the SQS mapping before those permissions are installed can fail Lambda's execution-role permission validation. Add an explicit dependency on the policy.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up enables queue consumption without waiting for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up_logging. With queued messages, the first invocation can run before logging permissions and the managed log group are ready. Make the mapping depend on this policy; its existing log-group reference also orders log-group creation.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger immediately invokes the syncer through the bucket notification, but does not wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. The current notification dependency ensures permission to invoke the Lambda, not the execution role's permission to write the runner distribution. Order this initial trigger after the S3 access policy to avoid a first-run authorization race.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger can invoke the syncer before module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging exists. The initial invocation can therefore lose its logs. Make the trigger depend on this policy, which already depends on the managed syncer log group, to ensure both logging permissions and the log group exist before the deployment-triggered execution.

When a customer-managed encryption key is configured, module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger can invoke the syncer before module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms grants its execution role access to that key. Neither the Lambda reference nor the notification dependency orders this policy. Make the deployment trigger depend on the optional policy collection so the initial encrypted distribution upload does not race KMS permissions.

When VPC subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role. The role ARN reference does not wait for its separate AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole attachment. Lambda can otherwise reject creation because its execution role cannot create network interfaces. Add depends_on on the attachment collection; this also keeps the VPC permissions attached until function destruction completes.

When VPC subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role. Referencing the execution role ARN does not order this separate policy attachment, so Lambda creation can race the EC2 network-interface permissions required for VPC access. Add depends_on on the attachment collection, also preserving it during VPC Lambda teardown.

When VPC subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_down must wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_down_vpc_execution_role. Its role ARN reference only waits for the IAM role, not attachment of the network-interface permissions Lambda validates for VPC provisioning. Add depends_on on the attachment collection, also preserving the permissions through function teardown.

When the pool is enabled with VPC subnets, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role. The shared IAM role reference does not order attachment of AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole; Lambda provisioning can therefore fail its network-interface permission checks. Add depends_on on this optional attachment collection, retaining it until the VPC Lambda has been destroyed.

When VPC subnets are configured, module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook must wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. Its role ARN reference does not include the separately attached VPC execution policy, allowing Lambda creation to run before the required network-interface permissions exist. Add depends_on on the attachment collection, also ensuring that the permissions remain during function teardown.

module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy is intended to install the dead-letter queue policy, but queue_url references queued_builds instead of module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq. When redrive is enabled this manages the main queue's policy twice and leaves the DLQ without its intended transport restriction. Reference the DLQ URL directly to attach the policy to the correct queue and infer the required dependency.

When Lambda subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role. Referencing the role ARN does not wait for its ENI-management permissions; creation can fail, and destruction can detach those permissions before VPC cleanup finishes. Add depends_on on the attachment.

When Lambda subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role. The role reference alone does not order the attachment supplying ENI-management permissions, risking failed VPC provisioning and premature permission removal during destruction.

When Lambda subnets are configured, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_down must wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_down_vpc_execution_role. VPC provisioning and cleanup require the attachment's ENI-management permissions, but the function's role reference does not order this attachment.

When the pool and its Lambda VPC configuration are enabled, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role. Otherwise Lambda can provision its VPC connection before ENI permissions are attached, or lose those permissions before cleanup on destruction.

When Lambda subnets are configured, module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_function.webhook must wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. The role ARN reference does not wait for the attachment granting ENI-management permissions needed for VPC provisioning and cleanup.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up must wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up, which grants its function access to the build queue. AWS validates the execution role's SQS polling permissions when creating the mapping. The existing function and queue references do not order this separately attached policy; add depends_on on the policy.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer can activate scheduled invocations before module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_lambda_permission.syncer allows EventBridge to invoke the function. Order the target after the permission to avoid failed deliveries during apply and to remove the target before revoking permission during destroy.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_permission.scale_down before activating the schedule. Both currently depend on the rule and function independently, so EventBridge can attempt invocation before it has permission.

When the pool is enabled, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_permission.pool. Otherwise the schedules can begin delivering events before EventBridge has permission to invoke the pool function.

module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue_policy.build_queue_dlq_policy is intended to secure module.runners:resource.aws_sqs_queue.queued_builds_dlq but currently assigns queue_url to the primary queue instead. Reference the DLQ URL so Terraform orders the policy after the correct queue and applies the policy to the intended destination.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger immediately triggers the initial binary synchronization, but does not wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer to grant the Lambda execution role S3 access. Waiting for the notification and invocation permission only authorizes S3 to invoke Lambda, not Lambda to write the distribution. Order the trigger after this policy to avoid a failed initial sync.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger can invoke the syncer before module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging is attached. Neither the trigger nor its notification dependency waits for this policy or the Terraform-managed log group it references. Wait for the logging policy before emitting the initial event so the initial sync can be logged.

When SSE-KMS is configured, module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger must wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms. Uploading the trigger starts synchronization immediately, and its kms_key_id reference configures the upload but does not wait for the Lambda role's separately attached KMS permissions. The initial sync can otherwise fail writing the encrypted distribution.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer enables a second invocation path independently of the on-deploy S3 trigger, but does not wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer. Order the scheduled target after the policy granting the syncer S3 access so scheduled synchronization cannot run before its execution permissions exist.

module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging before enabling invocations. This also waits for the log group referenced by that policy, ensuring scheduled executions can log from their first invocation.

When SSE-KMS is configured, module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for module.runners.module.runner_binaries:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms. The schedule otherwise can invoke the syncer before its execution role has permission to write the KMS-encrypted distribution.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down. The scheduled target can currently start invoking the function while its runtime permissions, including access to GitHub App parameters, are still being attached independently.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down_logging. That policy also depends on the managed log group; without this ordering, the every-minute schedule in this example can invoke scale-down before logging is ready.

When the pool is enabled, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool. The target currently enables pool adjustments before the execution role is guaranteed to have its EC2, SSM, and GitHub App parameter permissions.

When the pool is enabled, module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.pool should wait for module.runners.module.runners.module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging. Otherwise scheduled pool adjustments can begin before the logging policy and the log group it references are ready.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up is enabled by default and can immediately process queued jobs, but does not wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up_logging. Wait for that policy, which also waits for the managed log group, before enabling queue-driven executions.

module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app publishes the webhook URL to GitHub without waiting for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_apigatewayv2_stage.webhook. The URL is constructed from the API endpoint and a literal path, so its existing references do not establish stage readiness. Ensure the exported webhook endpoint carries a dependency on the stage before configuring GitHub, to avoid deliveries to an endpoint with no deployed stage.

module.webhook-github-app:resource.null_resource.update_app should wait for module.runners.module.webhook:resource.aws_lambda_permission.webhook before configuring GitHub to send events. The current exported endpoint does not depend on this permission, so GitHub can deliver while API Gateway is still unauthorized to invoke the Lambda. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner exposes the runner's SSM configuration directory through the ghr:ssm_config_path tag, but does not wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_config_run_as to populate that directory. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_agent_mode before it becomes usable by the scale-up and pool functions. The template points runner bootstrap at the SSM configuration directory only through a constructed tag string; this does not order creation of the agent_mode parameter consumed from that directory.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.jit_config_enabled. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_enable_cloudwatch. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_launch_template.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.token_path before runner launches are enabled downstream. module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_ssm_parameter.cloudwatch_agent_config_runner builds its default log-group names from locals rather than module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.gh_runners.
