The config object references the managed policy but not its attachment, so scheduled adjustments can execute before the pool role can read the AMI ID.

When create_service_linked_role_spot is enabled, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.service_linked_role. Queue-driven scale-up can otherwise run before the optional permission to create the Spot service-linked role is attached, defeating first-deployment Spot provisioning.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_parameters before being exposed to the launch template and runner-launching functions. Its role reference does not wait for the policy that lets runners read bootstrap configuration and registration tokens; early-launched instances can otherwise fail bootstrapping.

When the binary syncer is enabled, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dist_bucket. The profile's role reference does not order the separate S3-read policy, so downstream scale-up or pool executions can launch instances before those instances can download the cached runner distribution.

module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.describe_tags. The launch-template configuration supports metadata_tags disabled, in which case runner bootstrap needs DescribeTags access to discover its configuration tags. The role reference alone allows downstream launches before this separately attached policy exists.

When the CloudWatch agent is enabled, module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_instance_profile.runner should wait for module.runners.module.runners:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.cloudwatch. The launch template waits for the agent configuration parameter but not this policy granting the instance access to that configuration and logging APIs. Gate the profile's downstream use on the policy to avoid agent startup before permissions are attached.

When VPC subnets are configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role. Referencing the execution role ARN does not wait for AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole to be attached, so Lambda creation can race the attachment and fail because the role lacks EC2 network-interface permissions. Add depends_on on the attachment resource; the reverse destroy ordering also keeps these permissions attached during function deletion.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper references the role but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ami_housekeeper to install its application permissions. The enabled scheduled target can therefore invoke the function while the AMI housekeeping policy is still being installed, causing authorization failures. Order the function after this inline policy so its existing downstream trigger also waits for the policy.

When tracing is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.ami_housekeeper does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ami_housekeeper_xray. Its role reference orders only role creation, so the scheduled target can invoke the function before its X-Ray permissions are installed, losing initial traces. Add depends_on on the counted policy resource to order tracing permissions before the function and its downstream trigger.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ami_housekeeper can activate the enabled schedule before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging is installed, allowing invocations before logging is ready. Make the target depend on this policy, which already waits for the managed log group. Do not add that dependency to the Lambda function itself: the policy depends on the log group, which currently depends on the function, so that would introduce a cycle.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ami_housekeeper and :resource.aws_lambda_permission.ami_housekeeper currently share prerequisites but can be created concurrently. The target can begin delivering scheduled events before the permission allows events.amazonaws.com to invoke the function. Make the target depend on the permission so invocation authorization is installed first and retained until the target is removed during destruction.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.main should depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role when VPC networking is enabled. Referencing the execution role ARN does not wait for its VPC policy attachment, so Lambda creation can run before the role has the EC2 network-interface permissions required for VPC provisioning. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role]; this also preserves the attachment until function deletion completes.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.main does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging, so the function can become available to callers before its execution role can write logs. The role ARN reference waits only for role creation, not its inline policies. Establish ordering after the logging policy. First break the current reverse dependency: derive aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main.name from the same input-based function name instead of aws_lambda_function.main.function_name; otherwise adding this depends_on would create a cycle through the log group.

When tracing is enabled, :resource.aws_lambda_function.main should wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.xray. Both currently depend on the role independently, allowing the function to become available before the X-Ray permissions are installed and causing early invocations to lose traces. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy.xray]; depending on the counted resource also handles configurations where its count is zero.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.main should be ordered after :resource.aws_cloudwatch_log_group.main so its managed log group exists before the function becomes available for invocation. Currently the log group instead waits for the function; early invocations can encounter a missing group or auto-create it (the VPC execution policy grants logging permissions), racing Terraform's creation. Derive the log-group name directly from var.lambda.prefix and var.lambda.name to remove the reverse dependency, then order the function after the log group. Do not simply add depends_on to the current configuration, which would create a cycle.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.syncer_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured. Referencing the execution role does not wait for its managed-policy attachment; Lambda can attempt VPC provisioning without the required EC2 network-interface permissions. The dependency also keeps the policy attached until the function has been destroyed.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer, which grants its runner-distribution S3 access. Both resources depend on the role, but neither is ordered after the other. Because the deployment trigger can invoke the function immediately after creation, make the function wait for this policy so the initial sync cannot race policy installation.

When a customer-managed S3 KMS key is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer should wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_kms. The function's role reference does not order this separate policy, so the immediate deployment invocation can attempt encrypted S3 operations before the required KMS permissions are installed.

When tracing is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.syncer should wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.syncer_lambda_xray before becoming available to the deployment and scheduled triggers. Currently those triggers can invoke the function before its X-Ray permissions are installed, losing initial tracing data.

:resource.aws_s3_object.trigger immediately invokes the syncer through its S3 notification, but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging. That policy and the trigger can be created concurrently after the function exists, so the first invocation can run without logging permissions or the managed log group. Make the trigger wait for the logging policy, which already depends on the log group. Adding this dependency to the function instead would create a cycle with the current log-group configuration.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer can activate scheduled invocations before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging and its prerequisite log group are ready. Make the target wait for the logging policy so a schedule firing during apply cannot invoke the function without logging readiness. The existing function reference does not establish this ordering.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.syncer should wait for :resource.aws_lambda_permission.syncer before attaching the function to the enabled scheduled rule. Both resources reference the rule and function, but can be created concurrently; a schedule firing before the permission is installed can fail with an invocation authorization error.

When var.s3_versioning is Enabled, :resource.aws_s3_object.trigger can upload before :resource.aws_s3_bucket_versioning.action_dist has enabled versioning, and its notification can start the syncer's writes too early as well. Reference the versioning resource's bucket attribute to order the upload after versioning configuration. The provider documentation also recommends allowing 15 minutes after first enabling versioning before object writes; this ordering alone does not provide that propagation delay.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_up must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_up_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured. Referencing the execution role does not wait for its separately attached ENI permissions; Lambda creation can otherwise fail, and destruction can remove those permissions before Lambda finishes releasing its network interfaces. Add an explicit dependency on the attachment resource.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.scale_down must depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.scale_down_vpc_execution_role when deployed in a VPC. The role ARN reference does not order this separate attachment, so Lambda can attempt to provision network interfaces before the execution role has the required EC2 permissions. The dependency also preserves those permissions during function deletion.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.ssm_housekeeper must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ssm_housekeeper_vpc_execution_role when VPC subnets are configured. Both currently depend only on the role, allowing function creation to race attachment of the EC2 network-interface permissions required by Lambda. Add an explicit dependency, which also keeps the permissions attached through function deletion.

module.pool:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool needs module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role to complete before VPC-enabled function creation. Its role reference does not wait for that attachment, allowing Lambda to create network interfaces without the required EC2 permissions. Add an explicit dependency to order creation and preserve permissions during deletion.

module.job_retry.module.job_retry:resource.aws_lambda_function.main must depend on module.job_retry.module.job_retry:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.vpc_execution_role for VPC deployments. The execution-role reference alone does not wait for attachment of the ENI permissions needed during creation and deletion of a VPC-enabled Lambda.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up, which configures the execution role's access to the build SQS queue. AWS validates the role's queue-polling permissions when creating an SQS mapping; the function reference does not wait for this separately managed policy. The SQS aws_lambda_permission resource does not substitute for execution-role polling permissions.

module.job_retry:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.job_retry must wait for module.job_retry:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.job_retry to grant the execution role access to the retry queue. The queue and Lambda output references do not order this policy, so mapping creation can fail validation of SQS ReceiveMessage/DeleteMessage/GetQueueAttributes permissions. Add an explicit dependency on the role policy, not on the Lambda resource-based invocation permission.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down can enable scheduled invocations before :resource.aws_lambda_permission.scale_down authorizes EventBridge to invoke the function. Their common rule/function references do not order them. Make the target depend on the permission to avoid failed deliveries during deployment and to remove the target before revoking permission.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper can become active before :resource.aws_lambda_permission.ssm_housekeeper grants EventBridge invocation access. Add an explicit dependency from the target to the permission so scheduled cleanup deliveries are not attempted before authorization exists.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool references the scheduler role but does not wait for module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler to grant lambda:InvokeFunction. Schedules are enabled by default, so an invocation can race policy creation. Add an explicit dependency on the scheduler role policy.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down can start invoking the scale-down handler before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down grants its runtime AWS permissions. The function depends on the role, not this policy. Gate target activation on the policy so initial scheduled executions do not fail with AccessDenied.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper can activate before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_housekeeper grants the cleanup function access to SSM. Add a dependency on the policy at the event target, so cleanup is not scheduled before its runtime permissions are installed.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can invoke the pool handler before module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool grants its runtime EC2/SSM permissions. A reference to the Lambda function does not wait for its separate execution-role policy. Gate schedule creation on the policy.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up is enabled by default but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_up_logging. Queue processing can therefore start before logging permissions are installed. Depend on the logging policy at the mapping; this also orders the log group's creation without introducing the cycle that a function-to-logging-policy dependency would cause.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.scale_down does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scale_down_logging, allowing scheduled invocations before the log group and logging permissions are ready. Add the dependency at the target, not at the Lambda function, because the logging policy already depends transitively on the function.

:resource.aws_cloudwatch_event_target.ssm_housekeeper can trigger cleanup before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_housekeeper_logging and its log group exist. Gate the target on this logging policy to avoid unlogged initial executions; adding the reverse dependency at the function would create a cycle with the current log-group naming reference.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can invoke the pool Lambda before module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging installs logging permissions and completes the managed log group. Make the enabled schedule wait for the logging policy. This belongs on the schedule because the policy already depends transitively on the function.

module.job_retry:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.job_retry references a Lambda output containing the log group, but that output does not wait for module.job_retry.module.job_retry:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.lambda_logging. Queue processing can start without logging authorization. Gate the mapping on the child module's logging-policy readiness, for example by adding that policy to the child lambda output's depends_on.

When an external AMI-ID SSM parameter is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can start processing jobs before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read grants the scale-up function ssm:GetParameter access. The execution-role and launch-template references do not wait for this attachment. Gate the mapping on the attachment to prevent initial AMI lookup failures.

When an external AMI-ID SSM parameter is configured, module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can invoke the pool function before module.pool:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read grants access to that parameter. Passing the policy ARN through config orders policy creation, but not its attachment to the pool execution role. Make the schedule wait for the attachment.

When job retry is enabled, :resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can deliver jobs before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.job_retry_sqs_publish grants permission to publish retry-check messages. JOB_RETRY_CONFIG wires the queue into the function but does not order this separate permission policy. Add an explicit dependency on the policy at the mapping so the retry workflow is authorized before processing starts.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can begin launching runners before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_parameters grants the managed runner role access to bootstrap configuration and tokens. The launch template waits for the instance profile and role, but neither waits for this separate policy. When the module manages the runner role/profile, make scale-up activation wait for the policy so newly launched runners can read SSM immediately.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch runners before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.ssm_parameters grants their managed instance role access to bootstrap configuration and tokens. Passing the runner role and launch template into the pool module does not wait for the runner's separately installed policy. Gate pool activation on runner-policy readiness, for example through a dependency on that policy on the parent pool module.

With the binaries syncer enabled and the module managing the runner role, :resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can launch runners before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dist_bucket authorizes reading the S3 runner distribution used by the default installation user data. The instance-profile reference does not wait for the policy. Order scale-up activation after the policy to avoid runner installation failures.

With the binaries syncer enabled and a module-managed runner role, module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch instances before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.dist_bucket permits downloading the S3 runner distribution. The launch-template/role references do not wait for this separate policy. Gate pool scheduling on the policy, for example using a parent module dependency.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can start launching runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_config_run_as creates the run_as bootstrap setting. The configuration path is assembled from var.ssm_paths rather than resource references. Make scale-up activation wait for this parameter so a queued job cannot boot a runner against incomplete SSM configuration.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up does not wait for :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_agent_mode to establish the persistent/ephemeral bootstrap setting. A shared literal SSM path is not an ordering dependency. Gate the enabled mapping on the parameter so newly launched runners do not read configuration before it exists.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.disable_default_labels creates the runner label configuration under the SSM config path. There is no reference or dependency between them. Order mapping activation after this bootstrap parameter to avoid incomplete initial runner configuration.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can process jobs before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.jit_config_enabled creates the enable_jit_config bootstrap parameter. The Lambda/instance config paths are composed from variables, so Terraform cannot infer that runner startup needs this setting. Add an explicit dependency at the mapping.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_enable_cloudwatch establishes the CloudWatch-agent bootstrap flag. The shared SSM path provides no graph ordering. Gate mapping activation on this parameter so runners do not start with a partially populated configuration path.

:resource.aws_lambda_event_source_mapping.scale_up can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.token_path creates the bootstrap setting identifying the tokens/JIT-config path. The independently constructed path strings do not order parameter creation before queue processing. Make the enabled mapping wait for the token_path configuration parameter.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_config_run_as creates their run_as bootstrap setting. Passing a config path string into the pool module does not wait for this parameter. Order pool activation after parameter creation, for example with a dependency on the parameter on the parent pool module.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can invoke runner provisioning before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_agent_mode creates the persistent/ephemeral startup setting. No resource reference connects the configured SSM path to this parameter. Gate pool activation on parameter readiness, for example using a parent pool-module dependency.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch instances before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.disable_default_labels creates their label bootstrap setting. The module receives a path string rather than a reference to the parameter. Ensure pool scheduling waits for this parameter, for example with a dependency on the parent pool module.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can provision runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.jit_config_enabled establishes their JIT-mode bootstrap setting. The shared config path is not a dependency. Gate pool scheduling on creation of the parameter, for example through depends_on on the parent pool module.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.runner_enable_cloudwatch creates the agent-enable configuration setting. No ordering is inferred from the independently composed SSM path. Make pool activation wait for the parameter, for example through a dependency on the parent pool module.

module.pool:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can launch runners before :resource.aws_ssm_parameter.token_path creates the bootstrap setting that points to their token/JIT-config storage path. Passing SSM path strings to the pool module does not order this parameter. Gate pool scheduling on parameter readiness, for example with a parent pool-module dependency.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool must wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.pool_vpc_execution_role when VPC networking is configured. Referencing the execution role does not wait for its policy attachment; Lambda creation can otherwise fail because the role lacks permissions to create network interfaces. Add depends_on for the attachment resource.

:resource.aws_lambda_function.pool references its execution role but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool to install the runner-management permissions. The schedule can begin invoking the function before that policy is installed, causing authorization failures. Add depends_on for this policy so the function is not exposed to its downstream schedule before its required permissions are attached.

When tracing is enabled, :resource.aws_lambda_function.pool does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool_xray. Both depend on the role independently, so scheduled invocations can start before the X-Ray permissions are installed and fail to publish trace data. Add depends_on for the conditional policy resource.

When an AMI SSM parameter is configured, :resource.aws_lambda_function.pool does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.ami_id_ssm_parameter_read. The shared execution-role reference does not order policy attachment before function readiness, so initial scheduled invocations can lack access to the configured AMI parameter. Add depends_on for the attachment resource.

:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool is enabled by default but does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.scheduler, which grants its execution role lambda:InvokeFunction. Referencing the role ARN orders role creation only, allowing the schedule to activate before invocation permission is installed. Add depends_on for this policy.

:resource.aws_scheduler_schedule.pool can activate before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.pool_logging is installed, allowing invocations before the managed log group and its logging permissions are ready. Add depends_on for the logging policy on the schedule; that policy already depends on the log group. Ordering the schedule here avoids introducing a cycle through the log group's existing dependency on the Lambda function.

aws_lambda_function.webhook references the execution role but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. When lambda_subnet_ids is nonempty, Lambda needs the attached EC2 network-interface permissions to provision its VPC networking; function creation can race policy attachment and fail. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role], which also keeps these permissions attached until the function is destroyed.

aws_lambda_permission.webhook can enable API Gateway invocation before aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_logging is installed. The logging policy already waits for the function's log group, but neither it nor the log group is an ancestor of the invocation permission. Make the permission depend on this policy so initial requests do not race logging setup. Ordering at the permission avoids the cycle that a function-to-logging-policy dependency would create with the current log-group name reference.

aws_lambda_permission.webhook can enable API Gateway invocation while aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_sqs is still being installed. The webhook needs that policy to publish jobs to its configured SQS queues; the shared execution-role reference does not order policy installation before invocation becomes possible. Make the invocation permission depend on the SQS policy to avoid authorization failures on initial requests.

aws_lambda_permission.webhook does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_ssm, although the function reads its webhook secret and runner-matcher configuration from SSM. API Gateway can therefore invoke the function before its SSM access policy is installed. Make the invocation permission depend on this policy; referencing the execution role alone does not establish that ordering.

When config.kms_key_arn is configured for the webhook's KMS access, aws_lambda_permission.webhook can enable requests before aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_kms is installed, allowing initial requests that require the key to fail authorization. Make the invocation permission depend on the KMS policy so policy installation precedes API Gateway access.

When tracing is enabled, aws_lambda_permission.webhook can enable API Gateway invocation before aws_iam_role_policy.xray is installed. Initial invocations can consequently lack the configured X-Ray permissions and lose tracing data. Make the invocation permission depend on aws_iam_role_policy.xray; the dependency is harmless when the policy's count is zero.

aws_lambda_function.dispatcher references the execution role, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.dispatcher_vpc_execution_role. When lambda_subnet_ids is nonempty, Lambda needs the attached EC2 network-interface permissions during VPC provisioning; creating the function concurrently with the attachment can fail. Add depends_on on the attachment resource, also keeping it attached until function deletion completes.

aws_lambda_function.webhook references the execution role, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.webhook_vpc_execution_role. When lambda_subnet_ids is nonempty, Lambda needs the attached EC2 network-interface permissions during VPC provisioning; creating the function concurrently with the attachment can fail. Add depends_on on the attachment resource, also keeping it attached until function deletion completes.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.dispatcher can start routing events before aws_lambda_permission.allow_cloudwatch_to_call_lambda grants EventBridge permission to invoke the function. Both currently wait for the function and rule but not each other. Make the target depend on the permission to avoid an initial delivery-denial window and to remove the target before revoking permission during destruction.

aws_lambda_function.dispatcher does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_sqs. Its role reference orders only role creation, so EventBridge can invoke the deployed dispatcher before its queue-publishing permissions are installed. Add depends_on on the SQS role policy so initial dispatches do not race policy installation.

aws_lambda_function.dispatcher consumes runner-matcher configuration from SSM but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_ssm. The function and EventBridge target can become available before the execution role receives parameter-read permissions. Add depends_on on this policy to order policy installation before function availability.

When config.kms_key_arn is set, aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_kms supplies the dispatcher's configured KMS access, but aws_lambda_function.dispatcher has no dependency on that policy. Initial invocations can therefore race installation of the permissions needed for encrypted resources. Add depends_on on the KMS role policy.

When tracing is enabled, aws_lambda_function.dispatcher can become invokable before aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_xray installs the execution role's tracing permissions. The shared role reference does not order policy installation before the function. Add depends_on on the counted policy resource to avoid missing or denied initial trace submissions.

aws_lambda_function.webhook publishes to the event bus but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_eventbridge. Referencing the bus and role does not wait for the publishing policy, so API Gateway invocation permission can be granted while PutEvents is still unauthorized. Add depends_on on the publishing policy.

aws_lambda_function.webhook uses the webhook-secret SSM parameter but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_ssm to grant parameter access. The null_resource replacement trigger does not order IAM policy installation. Add depends_on on the SSM role policy so early webhook invocations do not race installation of secret-read permissions.

When config.kms_key_arn is set, aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_kms supplies the webhook's configured KMS access, but aws_lambda_function.webhook does not wait for that policy. Initial webhook requests can race installation of the permissions required to decrypt encrypted parameters. Add depends_on on the KMS role policy.

When tracing is enabled, aws_lambda_function.webhook can become invokable before aws_iam_role_policy.xray installs its execution role's tracing permissions. The role reference alone does not order these operations. Add depends_on on the counted policy resource to avoid missing or denied initial trace submissions.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.dispatcher can enable delivery before aws_iam_role_policy.dispatcher_logging grants logging access and, transitively, before the managed dispatcher log group exists. Make the target depend on the logging policy so initial invocations have their logging infrastructure ready. Ordering at the target avoids the cycle that a function-to-logging-policy dependency would introduce, because the policy already depends on the log group and function.

aws_lambda_permission.webhook can enable API Gateway invocations before aws_iam_role_policy.webhook_logging grants logging access and, transitively, before the managed webhook log group exists. Make the permission depend on the logging policy to prevent early invocations without logging readiness. Ordering at the permission avoids the cycle that a function-to-logging-policy dependency would introduce, because the policy already depends on the log group and function.

:resource.helm_release.certificate explicitly depends on :resource.helm_release.cert_manager, but that ordering is already established transitively through helm_release.cluster_issuer, which explicitly depends on cert_manager.
:resource.helm_release.kiali explicitly depends on :resource.kubectl_manifest.kube_prometheus_stack_operator_crds, but already depends on helm_release.istiod, which explicitly depends on those CRDs.

module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_key_id already references module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user.id. Its explicit depends_on on the same access key adds no ordering.

module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:output.access_secret_key already references module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_access_key.this_user.secret. Its explicit depends_on on the same access key adds no ordering.

:resource.helm_release.cluster_autoscaler starts a controller that calls AWS autoscaling/EC2 APIs, but has no ordering dependency on module.aws_iam_autoscaler:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. The role ARN output references only the IAM role, not its inline permissions policy. Wait for the IAM module's policy before deploying the controller (for example, depends_on = [module.aws_iam_autoscaler]), or add the policy to the role_arn output's depends_on.

:resource.helm_release.external_dns starts Route53 reconciliation, but does not wait for module.aws_iam_external_dns:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. The referenced role_arn output waits only for the role, allowing ExternalDNS to start before its permissions exist. Depend on the IAM module or make its role_arn output depend on this policy.

:resource.helm_release.cert_manager must have Route53 permissions for the subsequent ClusterIssuer/Certificate DNS validation workflow, but does not wait for module.aws_iam_cert_manager:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. Its role_arn reference waits only for the IAM role. Depend on the IAM module, or add the policy to its role_arn output's depends_on, so downstream certificate creation is ordered after policy installation.

:resource.helm_release.elk runs a Kibana init container that registers and verifies an S3 snapshot repository, which requires module.aws_iam_elastic_stack:resource.aws_iam_user_policy.this to be installed. Neither the credentials secret nor the access-key outputs wait for this user policy. Depend on the IAM module (and the credentials secret), or make the credential outputs depend on the user policy and wire the secret into the release.

:resource.helm_release.aws_loadbalancer_controller can start AWS reconciliation before module.aws_iam_aws_loadbalancer_controller:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this grants its EC2/ELB permissions. The role_arn output references only the role. Depend on the IAM module or make its role_arn output depend on the inline policy; this orders policy installation, although IAM propagation can still require retries.

:resource.helm_release.external_secrets begins polling SSM/Secrets Manager, but does not wait for module.aws_iam_external_secrets:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. Referencing the module's role_arn does not wait for its separate inline policy. Depend on the IAM module or add the policy to the role_arn output's depends_on to avoid startup authorization races.

:resource.helm_release.gitlab_runner enables S3 caching and ECR operations but does not wait for module.aws_iam_gitlab_runner:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. The module's role_arn output waits only for the role, not its permissions. Depend on the IAM module or make its role_arn output depend on the policy before starting the runner.

:resource.helm_release.prometheus_operator configures Grafana's CloudWatch datasource, but does not wait for module.aws_iam_kube_prometheus_stack_grafana:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. The role ARN alone does not establish ordering on this separate permissions policy. Depend on the IAM module or make its role_arn output depend on the policy to avoid initial CloudWatch authorization failures.

:resource.helm_release.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack configures Grafana's CloudWatch datasource, but does not wait for module.aws_iam_victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana:resource.aws_iam_role_policy.this. Its role_arn reference does not wait for the separate permissions policy. Depend on the IAM module or add the policy to its role_arn output's depends_on to avoid initial CloudWatch authorization failures.

:resource.helm_release.elk uses the literal Secret name elastic-credentials in Elasticsearch, Kibana and Beats configuration, but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials. Pods and init containers can start before credentials are available, and Terraform can delete the Secret before uninstalling the release. Reference the managed Secret name in the Helm values.

fix.expression: [local.elk_elasticsearch_values, local.elk_kibana_values, local.elk_filebeat_values, local.elk_apm_values, local.elk_metricbeat_values, yamlencode({ elasticsearch = { extraEnvs = [{ name = "ELASTIC_PASSWORD", valueFrom = { secretKeyRef = { name = kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials[count.index].metadata[0].name, key = "password" } } }, { name = "ELASTIC_USERNAME", valueFrom = { secretKeyRef = { name = kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_credentials[count.index].metadata[0].name, key = "username" } } }] } })]

message: :resource.helm_release.elk mounts the literal Secret name elastic-certificates but does not wait for :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates. Sharing the namespace dependency does not order the release after the certificate Secret. Wire its managed name into the Helm values to order Secret creation before consumers and destruction after them.

fix.expression: [local.elk_elasticsearch_values, local.elk_kibana_values, local.elk_filebeat_values, local.elk_apm_values, local.elk_metricbeat_values, yamlencode({ elasticsearch = { secretMounts = [{ name = "elastic-certificates", secretName = kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_certificates[count.index].metadata[0].name, path = "/usr/share/elasticsearch/config/certs" }] } })]

message: :resource.helm_release.elk configures its Elasticsearch keystore with the literal Secret name elasticsearch-s3-user-creds, but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds. The keystore initialization can race Secret creation. Use the managed Secret's metadata name in the keystore values.

fix.expression: [local.elk_elasticsearch_values, local.elk_kibana_values, local.elk_filebeat_values, local.elk_apm_values, local.elk_metricbeat_values, yamlencode({ elasticsearch = { keystore = [{ secretName = kubernetes_secret.elasticsearch_s3_user_creds[count.index].metadata[0].name, items = [{ key = "aws_s3_user_access_key", path = "s3.client.default.access_key" }, { key = "aws_s3_user_secret_key", path = "s3.client.default.secret_key" }] }] } })]

message: :resource.helm_release.elk uses the literal Secret name kibana-encryption-key for KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY, but does not wait for :resource.kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key. Reference the managed Secret name so Terraform orders Kibana deployment after Secret creation.

fix.expression: [local.elk_elasticsearch_values, local.elk_kibana_values, local.elk_filebeat_values, local.elk_apm_values, local.elk_metricbeat_values, yamlencode({ kibana = { extraEnvs = [{ name = "NODE_OPTIONS", value = "--max-old-space-size=800" }, { name = "ELASTICSEARCH_USERNAME", valueFrom = { secretKeyRef = { name = "elastic-credentials", key = "username" } } }, { name = "ELASTICSEARCH_PASSWORD", valueFrom = { secretKeyRef = { name = "elastic-credentials", key = "password" } } }, { name = "KIBANA_ENCRYPTION_KEY", valueFrom = { secretKeyRef = { name = kubernetes_secret.kibana_enc_key[count.index].metadata[0].name, key = "encryptionkey" } } }] } })]

message: :resource.helm_release.elk requests Elasticsearch persistent storage with the literal storageClassName advanced but has no dependency on :resource.kubernetes_storage_class.advanced. Helm waits for readiness by default, so volume provisioning can block while that independently scheduled StorageClass is absent. Reference the managed StorageClass name in the Helm values.

fix.expression: [local.elk_elasticsearch_values, local.elk_kibana_values, local.elk_filebeat_values, local.elk_apm_values, local.elk_metricbeat_values, yamlencode({ elasticsearch = { volumeClaimTemplate = { storageClassName = kubernetes_storage_class.advanced.metadata[0].name } } })]

message: :resource.helm_release.loki_stack enables persistence using the literal storageClassName advanced but does not wait for :resource.kubernetes_storage_class.advanced. Order the StorageClass before the release's PVC provisioning to avoid a readiness/installation race.

:resource.helm_release.prometheus_operator configures Prometheus volume claims with the literal storageClassName advanced, but has no ordering dependency on :resource.kubernetes_storage_class.advanced. Reference that managed name so storage provisioning is ordered after StorageClass creation.

fix.expression: concat(compact([local.kube_prometheus_stack_values, local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_values, local.istio.enabled ? local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_istio_values : null, local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_oauth_type == "gitlab" ? local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_gitlab_oauth_values : null, local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_oauth_type == "github" ? local.kube_prometheus_stack_grafana_github_oauth_values : null, local.kube_prometheus_stack_alertmanager_values, local.kube_prometheus_stack_alertmanager_slack_webhook != "" ? local.kube_prometheus_stack_alertmanager_slack_values : null]), [yamlencode({ prometheus = { prometheusSpec = { storageSpec = { volumeClaimTemplate = { spec = { storageClassName = kubernetes_storage_class.advanced.metadata[0].name } } } } } })])

message: :resource.helm_release.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack configures VMSingle persistent storage with the literal storageClassName advanced but does not wait for :resource.kubernetes_storage_class.advanced. Wire the managed StorageClass name into the values to order storage provisioning and preserve the correct reverse destruction order.

fix.expression: concat(compact([local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_values, local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_values, local.istio.enabled ? local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_istio_values : null, local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_oauth_type == "gitlab" ? local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_gitlab_oauth_values : null, local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_oauth_type == "github" ? local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_grafana_github_oauth_values : null, local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_alertmanager_values, local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_alertmanager_slack_webhook != "" ? local.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_alertmanager_slack_values : null]), [yamlencode({ vmsingle = { spec = { storage = { storageClassName = kubernetes_storage_class.advanced.metadata[0].name } } } })])

message: :resource.helm_release.cluster_autoscaler enables a ServiceMonitor explicitly placed in namespace monitoring, but only waits for its own workload namespace and the CRDs. When :module.kube_prometheus_stack_namespace supplies the monitoring namespace, its creation can race installation of that ServiceMonitor. Reference the enabled monitoring stack's namespace output instead of hard-coding monitoring.

:resource.helm_release.cluster_autoscaler creates its ServiceMonitor in the literal monitoring namespace, without waiting for :module.victoria_metrics_k8s_stack_namespace when VictoriaMetrics supplies that namespace. Waiting for CRDs does not wait for namespace creation. Wire the selected monitoring stack's namespace output into serviceMonitor.namespace.

aws_cloudtrail.main references the log bucket but does not wait for aws_s3_bucket_policy.cloudtrail to grant CloudTrail GetBucketAcl and PutObject permissions. Trail creation can race policy installation and fail with InsufficientS3BucketPolicyException. Use the policy's bucket attribute for s3_bucket_name to establish the missing ordering.

module.eventbridge creates enabled rules and SNS targets without waiting for aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts, which grants events.amazonaws.com permission to publish. Targets can become active before publication is authorized, causing initial alert delivery failures. Reading each topic ARN through its topic policy orders target creation after permission installation.

fix.expression: { for rule in ["secrets_manager_actions", "parameter_store_actions", "console_login_failed", "kms_cmk_delete_or_disable", "consolelogin_without_mfa", "unauthorized_api_calls", "usage_of_root_account", "iam_policy_changes", "cloudtrail_configuration_changes", "s3_bucket_policy_changes", "aws_config_changes", "security_group_changes", "nacl_changes", "network_gateway_changes", "route_table_changes", "vpc_changes", "organization_changes"] : rule => [{ name = "${replace(rule, "_", "-")}-notify-via-sns", arn = aws_sns_topic_policy.security_alerts[count.index].arn }] }

message: module.eks can launch self-managed workers before aws_ebs_encryption_by_default.default enables regional default encryption. Its block-device configuration sets encrypted = false, so initial volumes can be unencrypted if the regional default was previously disabled; enabling the default later does not encrypt existing volumes. Wire the managed encryption setting into the worker block-device configuration to establish ordering and explicitly request encryption.

fix.expression: { block_device_mappings = { xvda = { device_name = "/dev/xvda", ebs = { delete_on_termination = true, encrypted = aws_ebs_encryption_by_default.default.enabled, volume_size = 100, volume_type = "gp3" } } }, iam_role_additional_policies = var.eks_workers_additional_policies, metadata_options = { http_endpoint = "enabled", http_tokens = "required", http_put_response_hop_limit = 1, instance_metadata_tags = "disabled" }, iam_role_attach_cni_policy = false }

message: When enabled, module.pritunl launches an EC2 instance through its Auto Scaling group without explicit EBS encryption settings and without waiting for aws_ebs_encryption_by_default.default. If regional default encryption was previously disabled, initial instance volumes can be created unencrypted and are not retroactively encrypted. Add a dependency on the regional encryption setting at the root module.pritunl call so it is enabled before instances launch.

aws_eks_cluster.cluster references the cluster IAM role, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.cluster to attach its required EKS permissions. Add an explicit dependency so cluster creation cannot race policy attachment. The provider documentation explicitly requires ordering EKS cluster operations after its role permissions.

When control-plane logging is enabled, aws_eks_cluster.cluster can automatically create /aws/eks/${var.name_prefix}/cluster before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster creates the same group, causing ResourceAlreadyExistsException and bypassing the intended retention/encryption configuration. Make aws_eks_cluster.cluster wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster; their shared name_prefix and KMS references do not establish this ordering.

module.eks_node_group_al2023 uses aws_iam_role.eks_node_group.arn with create_iam_role=false, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.eks_node_group. That resource attaches the worker-node, CNI and ECR permissions needed for nodes to initialize and join the cluster. Order node-group creation after those policy attachments; referencing the role alone does not do so.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver references the service-account role but not aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.ebs_csi_controller_sa, which attaches AmazonEBSCSIDriverPolicy. Wait for that attachment before deploying the driver so its AWS operations do not initially fail with AccessDenied.

aws_eks_addon.adot references aws_iam_role.adot_collector but can start before aws_iam_role_policy_attachments_exclusive.adot_collector attaches its Prometheus, X-Ray and CloudWatch permissions. Make the add-on depend on that attachment so its configured service-account role is authorized before use.

aws_cloudwatch_event_target.karpenter_spot_interruption can activate event delivery before aws_sqs_queue_policy.karpenter_spot_interruption grants events.amazonaws.com permission to send messages. Depend on the queue policy so interruption-event delivery is authorized before the targets are installed; the existing queue ARN reference only waits for the queue.

aws_eks_addon.core_dns and module.eks_node_group_al2023 can be created concurrently after the control plane. CoreDNS runs Deployment pods and needs schedulable workers to become healthy; the add-on's ACTIVE-state wait can time out if node provisioning is delayed. Make the add-on wait for module.eks_node_group_al2023, the compute capacity configured in this project.

aws_eks_addon.aws_ebs_csi_driver has no ordering against module.eks_node_group_al2023. Its controller Deployment needs worker capacity to become healthy, so concurrent installation can leave the add-on waiting for pods and eventually timing out while workers are still provisioning. Make it depend on the node-group module.

aws_eks_addon.kubecost deploys workloads that require schedulable nodes, but only waits for the EKS control plane. Order it after module.eks_node_group_al2023 so the add-on health wait does not race creation of the project's worker capacity.

aws_eks_addon.adot installs an operator Deployment that needs worker capacity to become healthy. It currently can begin alongside module.eks_node_group_al2023 and time out waiting for unscheduled pods if node provisioning is delayed. Make the add-on depend on the node-group module.

aws_eks_addon.cloudwatch installs amazon-cloudwatch-observability, including operator workloads that require workers. Its cluster reference does not wait for module.eks_node_group_al2023. Order installation after that module to avoid racing the add-on's health wait against worker provisioning.

aws_eks_addon.snapshot_controller needs worker nodes for its controller Deployment to become healthy, but it can start as soon as the control plane exists. Add an ordering dependency on module.eks_node_group_al2023 so its add-on readiness wait does not race worker provisioning.

aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability waits for a log group and the control plane, but not for module.eks_node_group_al2023. Its operator workloads need schedulable workers to become healthy. Order the add-on after the node-group module to prevent its readiness wait from racing worker creation.

aws_eks_addon.metrics_server runs a Deployment requiring worker capacity, but has no dependency on module.eks_node_group_al2023. Make it wait for that module so add-on creation does not time out waiting for pods while the project's workers are still provisioning.

aws_eks_addon.kube_state_metrics needs schedulable workers for its Deployment to become healthy, but currently only waits for the control plane. Depend on module.eks_node_group_al2023 so the add-on's readiness wait cannot race creation of the configured worker capacity.

aws_eks_addon.cloudwatch starts CloudWatch observability agents that can automatically create the Container Insights performance log group. It does not wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_performance, which manages the same name. Order the add-on after that log group to avoid a ResourceAlreadyExistsException race and ensure Terraform's retention configuration is installed first.

aws_eks_addon.cloudwatch can start log collection before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application creates the matching Container Insights application group. The agents may auto-create that group, causing Terraform's creation to fail. Make the add-on wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application.

aws_eks_addon.cloudwatch can start log collection and auto-create the Container Insights dataplane group before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_dataplane manages it. Add an ordering dependency on that log group to prevent a same-name creation race and preserve the configured retention.

aws_eks_addon.cloudwatch can start log collection and auto-create the Container Insights host group before aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_host creates it. Make the add-on depend on that log group to avoid a ResourceAlreadyExistsException race.

aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability explicitly waits only for the performance log group. When aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application is enabled, the add-on's log collector can auto-create its matching application group first, causing Terraform's creation to fail. Also order the add-on after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_application.

aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability does not wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_dataplane. When that group is enabled, the add-on's log collector can auto-create the same dataplane group before Terraform, producing a creation conflict. Extend its dependencies to include aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_dataplane.

aws_eks_addon.amazon_cloudwatch_observability does not wait for aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_host. When that group is enabled, host-log collection can auto-create the same group before Terraform creates it, causing a ResourceAlreadyExistsException. Order the add-on after aws_cloudwatch_log_group.cluster_host as well as its existing performance-group dependency.

module.secure_baseline is configured for the organization management account, but has no dependency on aws_organizations_organization.org. Its organization data lookup can run before the organization exists, and its organization analyzers, organization trail and Config aggregator can run before ALL features and trusted service access are enabled. Add depends_on = [aws_organizations_organization.org] to the root module call.

aws_config_configuration_aggregator.organization references only aws_iam_role.config_organization, not aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.config_organization. The organization aggregator must wait for AWSConfigRoleForOrganizations to be attached so Config can retrieve organization details. Add an explicit dependency on the attachment, as in the provider's organization-aggregation example.

aws_cloudtrail.global references the CloudWatch delivery role but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy.cloudwatch_delivery_policy. Creating/configuring the trail can therefore race installation of logs:CreateLogStream and logs:PutLogEvents permissions, causing CloudWatch Logs authorization failures. Depend on the role policy before enabling delivery.

aws_cloudtrail.global references the SNS topic but does not wait for aws_sns_topic_policy.local-account-cloudtrail to grant cloudtrail.amazonaws.com sns:Publish. Trail creation/start can race the required topic authorization. Reference the policy's topic ARN to order creation after the policy.

data.aws_subnets.default in ap-northeast-1 reads default subnet inventory independently of aws_default_vpc.default. When no default VPC exists, the VPC resource creates it and its default subnets during apply, after this lookup may already have returned an empty set; the subnet-hardening resources then miss those subnets. Order the lookup after the default VPC. An idiomatic implementation is an additional filter block: filter { name = "vpc-id"; values = [aws_default_vpc.default.id] } (use separate HCL lines, not semicolons).

aws_ecs_service.this uses the infrastructure role in vpc_lattice_configurations, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy. Referencing the role does not ensure its VPC Lattice permissions are attached. Add this attachment to depends_on so ECS cannot configure Lattice before the permissions exist, and the permissions remain attached until service deletion completes.

aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition uses the infrastructure role in vpc_lattice_configurations, but does not wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.infrastructure_iam_role_vpc_lattice_policy. The existing dependencies cover the service policy and EBS policy, not the Lattice policy. Add this attachment to depends_on to order Lattice permissions before service creation and preserve them through service deletion.

aws_ecs_task_definition.this waits for external task-role policies and execution-role policies, but omits aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.tasks_internal, which supplies ECS Exec and custom task-role permissions. The task_role_arn reference orders only role creation, not this attachment. Include tasks_internal in the existing depends_on gate so services and task sets consuming the definition cannot launch tasks before these permissions are attached; this is a runtime ordering requirement, not a task-definition registration requirement.
:data.aws_ecs_task_definition.this explicitly depends on :resource.aws_ecs_task_definition.this, but task_definition = aws_ecs_task_definition.this[0].family already establishes that dependency.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this can launch tasks before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec attaches the execution policy. Referencing the execution role through the task definition does not wait for its policy attachment; order service creation after this attachment so initial tasks have ECR, logging, and configured secret-access permissions.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition can launch tasks before :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec attaches the execution policy. Ignoring task_definition changes does not remove the initial deployment's need for ECR, logging, and configured secret-access permissions; order service creation after this attachment.

When additional execution policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.this has no ordering dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec_additional. Tasks may launch before those execution permissions are attached, causing initialization failures for workloads that require them. Wait for these attachments before deploying the service.

When additional execution policies are configured, :resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition has no ordering dependency on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.task_exec_additional. Its initial tasks may launch before the execution permissions they require are attached. Wait for these attachments before deploying the service.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.this does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks. When ECS Exec or custom task-role statements are enabled, tasks and their Exec agent can start before the corresponding permissions are installed. The task-role ARN reference orders role creation, not this inline policy; add ordering on the policy.

:resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition does not wait for :resource.aws_iam_role_policy.tasks. When ECS Exec or custom task-role statements are enabled, initial tasks and their Exec agent can start before the corresponding permissions are installed. Ignoring task-definition changes does not establish ordering on this inline policy.

A task-role reference does not wait for these attachments. Order deployment after them to avoid startup-time AccessDenied failures.

A task-role reference does not wait for these attachments; order service deployment after them.

For awsvpc deployments using the module-created security group, :resource.aws_ecs_service.this does not wait for :resource.aws_security_group_rule.this. Terraform removes the group's default allow-all egress rule, so starting tasks before configured egress/ingress rules exist can break image pulls, secret retrieval, or health checks. Order service deployment after these rules.

For awsvpc deployments using the module-created security group, :resource.aws_ecs_service.ignore_task_definition does not wait for :resource.aws_security_group_rule.this. Security-group existence alone does not ensure configured traffic is allowed; initial tasks can fail initialization or health checks while the separate rules are still being created. Order deployment after the rules.

aws_ecs_cluster_capacity_providers.this must wait for aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this to create the autoscaling capacity providers before associating their names with the cluster. The supplied graph contains no such dependency, and capacity_providers uses input names rather than the created resources. Reference the created capacity providers' names to establish the ordering.

fix.expression: distinct(concat([for k, v in var.fargate_capacity_providers : try(v.name, k)], [for k, v in aws_ecs_capacity_provider.this : v.name]))

message: aws_eks_node_group.this must wait for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this, not merely for the IAM role. These attachments supply the worker-node, ECR, and optional CNI permissions needed by the nodes. The supplied graph has no dependency path enforcing this ordering. Add depends_on so permissions exist before node-group creation and remain attached until node-group deletion completes, as required by the provider's documented example.

aws_eks_node_group.this has no dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional. When additional node-role policies are configured, nodes and their workloads can start before those permissions are attached, and the policies can be detached before the nodes and workloads finish shutting down. Add depends_on on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional to preserve these permissions throughout the node-group lifecycle; the launch template's existing dependency covers only aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this.

aws_autoscaling_group.this can launch self-managed EKS nodes before aws_eks_access_entry.this authorizes their instance role. Neither sharing the IAM role nor referencing the cluster inputs orders these operations. When create_access_entry is enabled, make the Auto Scaling group depend on the access entry so node bootstrap does not race cluster authentication setup and the entry remains until the group is destroyed. This establishes ordering, not a guarantee of immediate authentication propagation.

aws_launch_template.this explicitly waits for aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.this to keep node-dependent permissions available during create/destroy, but omits aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional. The additional attachments and launch template can proceed independently after the role exists. When additional policies supply bootstrap or workload permissions, nodes can start before those permissions are attached, and the policies can be detached before nodes terminate. Extend the existing dependency guard to aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional.

null_resource.wait_for_cluster explicitly depends on aws_eks_cluster.this, but its local-exec environment already references aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint. That reference establishes the same ordering; remove only the cluster entry, retaining the dependency on cluster_private_access.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch nodes before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy completes. Referencing the instance profile does not order the separate policy attachment. Depend on this attachment so worker API permissions are installed before bootstrap and retained until the group is destroyed.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch nodes before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy completes. When this optional attachment is managed, order the group after it so the aws-node CNI has its networking permissions during node initialization; referencing the role or instance profile does not establish that ordering.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers has no ordering dependency on aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly. Nodes can start pulling EKS system images before their ECR permissions are attached. Order group creation after the attachment and its destruction before policy removal.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template can launch nodes before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy completes. The launch-template instance-profile reference does not order the separate policy attachment. Depend on this attachment so worker API permissions exist before bootstrap and remain through group destruction.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template can launch nodes before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKS_CNI_Policy completes. When this optional attachment is managed, order the group after it so the aws-node CNI has its networking permissions during node initialization; a launch-template reference does not order this attachment.

Nodes can start pulling EKS system images before their ECR permissions are attached. Order group creation after the attachment and its destruction before policy removal.

:data.http.wait_for_cluster already depends on :resource.aws_eks_cluster.this through its url and ca_certificate expressions. Its explicit depends_on entry for the cluster adds no ordering and can be removed; retain the dependency on the private-access rule.

module.fargate:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this is not ordered after module.fargate:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.eks_fargate_pod. Referencing the execution role does not ensure AmazonEKSFargatePodExecutionRolePolicy is attached before Fargate uses it, or retained until the profile is deleted. When the Terraform runner reaches the private Kubernetes endpoint using one of the configured source security groups, the health check can start before its ingress permission exists. Include this rule in the health check's depends_on.

:resource.aws_eks_cluster.this waits for the managed cluster policies but not :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.cluster_elb_sl_role_creation. This attachment supplies control-plane permissions for ELB provisioning; without an ordering edge it is not guaranteed to be installed before the cluster is exposed to consumers or retained throughout cluster teardown. Include it with the other cluster IAM policy dependencies.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers waits for the three standard worker policies but not :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_additional_policies. For groups using the default worker role, additional permissions can therefore be attached after nodes start or detached before their workloads finish draining. Add this attachment collection to the parent module's ng_depends_on list, as already done for the self-managed workers.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers has no ordering dependency on :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_egress_internet. When a managed group uses the module-created launch template and worker security group, nodes need this egress permission for bootstrapping and ongoing API/image access. Include the rule in the parent's ng_depends_on list so it is installed before node provisioning and retained until node-group deletion finishes.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers is not ordered after :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_ingress_self. Managed groups using the custom launch template's worker security group require this rule for node/pod communication; the security group ID alone does not wait for its rules. Include this rule in the parent's ng_depends_on list to preserve connectivity throughout provisioning and teardown.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers does not depend on :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_ingress_cluster. For managed groups using the custom launch template's worker security group, this rule supplies control-plane-to-worker connectivity, but can currently be created after nodes launch or removed during draining. Include it in the parent's ng_depends_on list, matching the ordering used for self-managed workers.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers has no dependency on :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_ingress_cluster_kubelet. When worker_sg_ingress_from_port exceeds 10250, this separate rule provides the control plane's kubelet access for managed nodes using the custom worker security group. Include it in the parent's ng_depends_on list so that access is established before provisioning and retained through deletion.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers does not wait for :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_ingress_cluster_https. For managed nodes using the custom worker security group, extension API servers/webhooks on port 443 depend on this control-plane ingress rule. Add it to the parent's ng_depends_on list so these workloads do not lose access before node-group draining completes, consistent with self-managed worker ordering.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers is not ordered after :resource.aws_security_group_rule.workers_ingress_cluster_primary. When primary-security-group interoperability is enabled and managed nodes use the custom worker security group, this rule permits traffic from Fargate/primary-group workloads. Include it in the parent's ng_depends_on list to establish connectivity before nodes run and keep it until node-group teardown completes.

module.node_groups:resource.aws_eks_node_group.workers does not depend on :resource.aws_security_group_rule.cluster_primary_ingress_workers. When primary-security-group interoperability is enabled, managed nodes using the custom worker security group need this rule to reach Fargate/primary-group workloads. Include it in the parent's ng_depends_on list, as for self-managed workers, so connectivity is ready before node provisioning and maintained through draining.

null_resource.wait_for_cluster already depends implicitly on aws_eks_cluster.this through the ENDPOINT environment variable in its local-exec provisioner. Its explicit depends_on entry for the cluster duplicates that ordering and can be removed.

When the module creates the worker security group, order the ASG after this egress rule to avoid blocking bootstrap access to AWS APIs and container registries.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template can launch instances before aws_security_group_rule.workers_egress_internet permits outbound traffic. When the module creates the worker security group, order the ASG after this egress rule to avoid blocking bootstrap access to AWS APIs and container registries.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers does not wait for aws_security_group_rule.cluster_https_worker_ingress, which permits worker-to-control-plane HTTPS traffic. When workers use the private endpoint and the module-managed cluster security group, they can begin registration before the required ingress exists. Order the ASG after this rule; references to the cluster and security-group IDs do not wait for rule creation.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers_launch_template does not wait for aws_security_group_rule.cluster_https_worker_ingress, which permits worker-to-control-plane HTTPS traffic. When workers use the private endpoint and the module-managed cluster security group, they can begin registration before the required ingress exists. Order the ASG after this rule; references to the cluster and security-group IDs do not wait for rule creation.

null_resource.wait_for_cluster already references aws_eks_cluster.this[0].endpoint in its local-exec environment, which establishes the cluster dependency implicitly. Its explicit depends_on on aws_eks_cluster.this duplicates that ordering and can be removed.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch nodes using the module-managed worker role before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEKSWorkerNodePolicy completes. Depend on the attachment to avoid initializing node networking without its required permissions.

aws_autoscaling_group.workers can launch instances before aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.workers_AmazonEC2ContainerRegistryReadOnly completes. When this policy is managed on the worker role, instances can initialize the VPC CNI before its required permissions have been attached. The existing dependency on those attachments is only on the optional launch template; with create_launch_template=false it does not protect the node group. Put the attachment dependency on the node group itself, as recommended in the provider documentation.

When IPv6 CNI policy creation and attachment are enabled, :module.eks_managed_node_group attaches the policy created by :resource.aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy using an independently constructed ARN. Nothing orders policy creation before the child module's attachments, so AttachRolePolicy can fail with NoSuchEntity. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy] to the module call.

When IPv6 CNI policy creation and attachment are enabled, :module.self_managed_node_group attaches the policy created by :resource.aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy using an independently constructed ARN. Nothing orders policy creation before the child module's attachments, so AttachRolePolicy can fail with NoSuchEntity. Add depends_on = [aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy] to the module call.

For a configured add-on using service_account_role_arn, :resource.aws_eks_addon.this requires the cluster's IAM OIDC provider, :resource.aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.oidc_provider, to exist before its pods can use IRSA. The provider documentation explicitly requires an OIDC provider for this setting, but these resources currently run independently after cluster creation. Order compute-dependent add-ons after this module when it supplies their nodes; keep any add-ons required before node bootstrap in a separate pre-compute resource.

Order compute-dependent add-ons after this module when it supplies their nodes; keep any add-ons required before node bootstrap in a separate pre-compute resource.

Depend on the attachment set to establish creation ordering and retain permissions through profile deletion.

module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_eks_fargate_profile.this does not wait for module.fargate_profile:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional. Configured additional execution-role permissions can therefore be absent when matching Fargate pods start, or be detached before profile teardown. Include these attachments in the profile's depends_on alongside its required policy attachments.

module.self_managed_node_group:resource.aws_launch_template.this waits for the standard role-policy attachments but not module.self_managed_node_group:resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.additional. This leaves the documented policy-readiness barrier incomplete: instances using this template can start workloads before their additional node-role permissions are attached, and those permissions can disappear prematurely during teardown. Include the additional attachment set in the existing depends_on.

:resource.aws_eks_cluster.this does not depend on :resource.aws_iam_role_policy_attachment.cluster_encryption. When attach_cluster_encryption_policy is enabled, the cluster's KMS permissions can be attached concurrently with cluster creation and detached before cluster teardown. Add this attachment to the cluster's depends_on so its configured encryption permissions are available for the cluster lifecycle; the key ARN reference alone does not order this separate attachment.

:module.eks_managed_node_group should depend on :resource.aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy when this project creates the IPv6 CNI policy. The child module reconstructs the policy ARN from the account ID and literal AmazonEKS_CNI_IPv6_Policy name instead of receiving a reference to the policy resource, so its role-policy attachment can run before that policy exists and fail with NoSuchEntity. Add a module-level depends_on to order these operations and prevent premature policy deletion.

:module.self_managed_node_group should depend on :resource.aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy when this project creates the IPv6 CNI policy. The child module builds its ARN from the account ID and hard-coded policy name; this does not order its role-policy attachment after policy creation. Add a module-level depends_on to prevent attachment failures and deletion of the policy before its attachments are removed.

:module.fargate_profile should depend on :resource.aws_iam_policy.cni_ipv6_policy when the project creates that policy and the profile attaches it. The child module constructs the IPv6 policy ARN using the literal AmazonEKS_CNI_IPv6_Policy name, so its IAM attachment can race policy creation. Add a module-level depends_on to establish creation and reverse destruction ordering.

:resource.aws_eks_addon.this has no dependency on :resource.aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.oidc_provider. For add-ons configured with service_account_role_arn, the provider documentation requires an IAM OIDC provider for the cluster; the supplied role ARN does not establish ordering against this locally created provider. Add depends_on so IRSA-enabled add-ons are not installed before their OIDC provider exists or retained after it is deleted.
